```

title: Validation steps sometimes do not align in the multiagent
description:
## Problem

In the multiagent, we expect validation steps to align when they are equivalent in form (i.e., identical function calls). For example, four agents below all share the `col_vals_not_null(c)` step and the hash for this step is shared, regardless of when/where the step is added to the agent:

```r
library(pointblank)
agent <- create_agent(small_table)

agent_global1 <- agent %>% 
  col_vals_not_null(c) %>% 
  interrogate()
agent_global2 <- agent %>% 
  col_vals_not_null(c) %>% 
  interrogate()
agent_local1 <- local({
  agent %>% 
    col_vals_not_null(c) %>% 
    interrogate()
})
agent_local2 <- local({
  agent %>% 
    col_vals_not_null(c) %>% 
    interrogate()
})
create_multiagent(agent_global1, agent_global2, agent_local1, agent_local2) %>% 
  get_multiagent_report(display_mode = "wide")
```

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/assets/52832839/b1f7a465-25ca-4d4b-8108-82b54be4cb79)

However, the same step defined in different environments fail to align when they involve special data structures that record the environment. This is the case for:
1) Functions passed to `preconditions`, when the function is defined inline (e.g., using the magrittr syntax `. %>% ...`)

```r
agent_local_precondition <- local({
  small_table %>% 
    create_agent() %>% 
    col_vals_not_null(c, preconditions = . %>% identity()) %>% 
    interrogate()
})
agent_global_precondition <- small_table %>% 
  create_agent() %>% 
  col_vals_not_null(c, preconditions = . %>% identity()) %>% 
  interrogate()
create_multiagent(agent_local_precondition, agent_global_precondition) %>% 
  get_multiagent_report(display_mode = "wide")
```

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/assets/52832839/8b5bbc26-ab0f-4cef-818c-1931adbf27f0)

- Quosures (i.e., `vars()`) passed to `values`

```r
agent_local_vars <- local({
  small_table %>% 
    create_agent() %>% 
    col_vals_gt(c, value = vars(a)) %>% 
    interrogate()
})
agent_global_vars <- small_table %>% 
  create_agent() %>% 
  col_vals_gt(c, value = vars(a)) %>% 
  interrogate()
create_multiagent(agent_local_vars, agent_global_vars) %>% 
  get_multiagent_report(display_mode = "wide")
```

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/assets/52832839/fdf4ea06-0094-4b38-965a-7e0547e7ce3e)

This raises two concerns:
1. Hashing can be overly strict, in ways that may be unpredictable for the user (especially in real world scenarios where agents are defined months or years apart in different workspaces and setups).
2. Hashing the environment can cause severe performance problems when large objects are involved (#508)

## Possible remedy

1. Resolve such complex data structures to string before they're passed to `digest::sha1()`, to avoid hashing the environment
2. Build in a (opt-in or fallback) mechanism for backwards compatibility to account for (1), such as by having the multiagent re-generate the hash for every step for the purposes of alignment

title: Cryptic performance bug with hashing
description:
## Problem

During the validation planning step, there is some weird stateful bug going on with `digest::sha1()` here that creates an unexpected performance bottleneck:

https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/blob/7c4bdd0eb753db17b5213d03fd74f044df12be48/R/steps_and_briefs.R#L45-L66

It's a bit hard to explain because I don't completely understand this myself (in fact, this may be a downstream issue with digest), so I'll just show the reprex first.

## Reprex

Suppose we have a 10-thousand row, 30 column dataframe. 

```r
library(pointblank)
tbl <- as.data.frame(replicate(30, rnorm(1e5)))
dim(tbl)
#> [1] 10000    30
```

We can run a trivial set of validations where for each column, we compare its value to the first column. And for some reason maybe we also just care about the first row. We can loop over columns with `columns = everything()`, and this runs fast: 

```r
system.time({
  agent <- create_agent(tbl)
  agent %>% 
    col_vals_gte(
      columns = everything(),
      value = vars(V1),
      preconditions = . %>% head(1)
    )
})
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.36    0.00    0.44
```

One might instead prefer to explicitly for-loop over a set of columns for finer control (e.g., to compare pairs of columns). But this now suddenly takes magnitudes longer:

```r
system.time({
  agent <- create_agent(tbl)
  for (col in colnames(tbl)) {
    agent <- agent %>% 
      col_vals_gte(
        columns = col,
        value = vars(V1),
        preconditions = . %>% head(1)
      )
  }
})
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 9.20    1.67   11.87 
```

This by the way isn't an artifact of the for loop structure - if you remove `preconditions` and set `value` to a constant like `1`, then the performance difference goes away:

```r
system.time({
  agent <- create_agent(tbl)
  agent %>% 
    col_vals_gte(
      columns = everything(),
      value = 1
    )
})
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>    0.33    0.00    0.35
```

When I profiled the slow method, it unexpectedly picked up on `digest::sha1()` being the problem. So it's something about hashing the values for `value` (when it's a quosure) and `preconditions`

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/assets/52832839/8f79db72-13b8-4f10-954e-73fb5a677213)

One final thing I discovered before hitting a wall is that the internal call to `sha1()` gets progressively slower with each validation added to the agent. Here's what I get from running the same slow method, but with the call to `sha1()` wrapped in `system.time()` (so it's timed 30 times, once for each validation step):

<details>
<summary>Timing for each validation step's call to `sha1()`</summary>

```r
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.02    0.00    0.03 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.03    0.00    0.04 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.06    0.00    0.06 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.04    0.00    0.08 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.06    0.00    0.09 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.08    0.00    0.12 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.11    0.00    0.14 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.11    0.07    0.17 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.18    0.01    0.21 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.03    0.00    0.31 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.17    0.03    0.27 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.22    0.05    0.29 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.22    0.06    0.32 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.25    0.05    0.33 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.28    0.01    0.36 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.33    0.02    0.37 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.26    0.06    0.41 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.34    0.05    0.40 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.36    0.09    0.47 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.33    0.09    0.49 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.39    0.08    0.49 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.44    0.06    0.54 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.45    0.08    0.56 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.43    0.09    0.59 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.50    0.08    0.58 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.55    0.06    0.68 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.46    0.15    0.68 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.49    0.11    0.74 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.53    0.08    0.73 
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.52    0.16    0.75
```

</details>

Adding a 31st validation step to this agent will follow this same performance trend. But again, it's only the case when it involves hashing `vars()` or a `preconditions` function:

```r
agent %>% col_vals_between(columns = V2, left = vars(V1), right = vars(V3))
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0.70    0.21    0.85 

agent %>% col_vals_between(columns = V2, left = 0, right = 1)
#> user  system elapsed 
#> 0       0       0
```

My suspicion with what's happening here is that the the *environment* is also being hashed: the behavior that we're seeing appears to be somewhat stateful (takes longer to hash later validation steps) and it only happens when we're hashing R objects with environments attached to them (quosures and functions).

In fact, I actually think that continuing to pass the environment down for hashing could cause some weird bugs down the line. For example, The same validation step in the example below are actually different in hash because the preconditions function is defined in different environments:

```r
library(pointblank)

# Precondition's env is global env
agent1 <- create_agent(small_table) %>% 
  col_vals_not_null(a, preconditions = . %>% head(1))

# Precondition's env is local function env
f <- function(x) {
  x %>% 
    col_vals_not_null(a, preconditions = . %>% head(1))
}
agent2 <- create_agent(small_table) %>% 
  f()

agent1$validation_set$sha1
#> [1] "d04c090bd37b3b6ec81243bb82ba8fd28544d63d"
agent2$validation_set$sha1
#> [1] "afdf459bf50aeed3c9397479f992e65a1db92b77"
```

Again, I realize that it's tricky to update the hashing logic for backwards compatibility, but one simple way out of this is to resolve complex R objects to string before passing them to `digest::sha1()`. If we could just wrap `values` and `preconditions` in something like `deparse1()`, it would still create unique identifiers for validation steps while resolving the performance (and unexpected env related) issues.

I'd be happy to look into supporting backwards compatibility in places where this matters (which I think is used just for aligning validations steps in the multiagent, if I understand correctly?). Thanks for considering!

title: Support `where()` predicates for tidyselect in `info_columns()`
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **pointblank**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/issues) (both open and closed).

## Problem

Currently, `columns` in `info_columns()` does have the new/complete tidyselect backend, but cannot utilize the `where()` helper:

```r
informant <- create_informant(small_table)
# Works
informant %>% 
  info_columns(starts_with("date"), info = "Data about a time point")
# Should do the same thing but doesn't work
informant %>% 
  info_columns(where(lubridate::is.timepoint), info = "Data about a time point")
#> Warning message:
#> No columns were matched with the expression used, so, no info was added. 
```

This is because columns are resolved against this dummy data that's re-generated from the column names:

https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/blob/70c2075b4d7ba0434a4e27a159d52cfa051ebdd7/R/info_add.R#L450-L455

Where the `x` looks like the following:

```r
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   date_time  date     a     b     c     d     e     f
#>       <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1         1     1     1     1     1     1     1     1
```

## Proposal

I have two ideas:

1) Only resolve against the dummy data if the data is read directly (i.e., `informant$tbl` is not NULL). This is super simple - we can just `if`-case the above lines from `info_columns()`. (Now in #503)

This is good, but not perfect - it means that the support for `where()` is not extended to databases and even simple cases like:

```r
create_informant(~small_table)$tbl
#> NULL
```

2) Have the informant store information about **column prototypes**, to at least support `is.<class>` predicates in `where()`. (Now in #504 )

I think this could be a good middle ground that doesn't break the laziness/lightweight-ness of informants. Essentially, the proposal is to add an extra bit of information to the informant which is just the dataframe *header*, like:

```r
head(small_table, 0)
#> # A tibble: 0 × 8
#> # ℹ 8 variables: date_time <dttm>, date <date>, a <int>, b <chr>, c <dbl>, d <dbl>, e <lgl>, f <chr>
```

We don't have to execute an extra query for this. We can do it all in one go here, at the informant's creation:

https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/blob/70c2075b4d7ba0434a4e27a159d52cfa051ebdd7/R/utils.R#L746-L763

The proposal is for this function to also return information about the prototypes (`col_ptypes`). So something like:

```r
get_r_column_names_types <- function(tbl) {
  
  suppressWarnings(
    column_header <-
      tbl %>%
      utils::head(1) %>%
      dplyr::collect()
  )
  column_names_types <-
    vapply(column_header, function(x) class(x)[1], character(1))
  
  list(
    col_names = names(column_names_types),
    r_col_types = unname(unlist(column_names_types)),
    col_ptypes = utils::head(column_header, 0)
  )
}
```

Then we can string this 0-row `col_ptypes` dummy data along for tidyselect purposes. The one tricky part is that this info needs to be invisible to gt-rendering/yaml-writing, but I think this could also serve as an opportunity to build in a `$_private`-like property to the informant for future extensibility.

It's overall a small surgery but does touch multiple behaviors, so I'd like to hear your thoughts first. The hope is to get something like below working. LMK what you think!

```r
create_informant(~ small_table) %>% 
  info_columns(
    columns = where(lubridate::is.timepoint),
    info = "Data about a time point"
  )
```
![image](https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/assets/52832839/cd066602-d91c-41a5-b265-80d554be35ca)

title: Better handling for bad column selections
description:
I think the skipping behavior with `columns = NULL` on the `col_vals_*()`/`col_is_*()` functions is new. I tried setting `columns = NULL` with `main` (before the 2 PRs) and got an ugly error, which is undocumented and shouldn't really happen when using an agent.

If you're up for it, this would be another chance for modernization of the API to use more tidyselect semantics. Right now in `main`, `columns = NULL` results in a single, skipped validation step. That's better than before but I'm not certain it's what we want. We have an `active` argument that is better meant for that, where we could supply a logical or a function that should resolve to a logical (which I believe is in the same/similar scope as a function invoked as `preconditions`; the helper function is `has_columns()` and this is the PR that introduces it: https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/pull/240). This work (should you choose to accept it!) can all be deferred to a non-documentation PR.

Here are some examples, and I'll summarize what happens with `main`:

```r 
create_agent(exibble) |>
  col_vals_lt(columns = NULL, value = 5) |>
  interrogate()
```

^ skips. Probably not ideal, you get a weird autobrief (`"Expect that values in NA (computed column) ... "`)

```r
create_agent(exibble) |>
  col_vals_lt(columns = starts_with("z"), value = 5) |>
  interrogate()
```

^ same result as before but more likely for the user to hit. It can be dangerous safety-wise to use tidyselect because the match can be arbitrary. Users should be advised to pair with a `has_columns()` check in the `active` argument.

```r
create_agent(exibble) |>
  col_vals_lt(columns = num,  value = 5, active = ~ . %>% has_columns(num)) |>
  interrogate()
```

^ this ought to work but tidyselect is not yet ported to `active`/`has_columns()`. So we get a console error with `interrogate()` (the error is not captured internally); we don't get a full validation report.

```r
create_agent(exibble) |>
  col_vals_lt(columns = num, value = 5, active = ~ . %>% has_columns("num")) |>
  interrogate()
```
```r
create_agent(exibble) |>
  col_vals_lt(columns = num, value = 5, active = ~ . %>% has_columns(vars(num))) |>
  interrogate()
```

^ The above two cases (with string-based column names or with `vars()`) work as before.

```r
create_agent(exibble) |>
  col_vals_lt(columns = starts_with("z"), value = 5, active = ~ . %>% has_columns(starts_with("z"))) |>
  interrogate()
```

^ doesn't work, but closer to a safety net that is useful.

This is a lot to sort though, so let me know if more work in this direction is worthwhile!

_Originally posted by @rich-iannone in https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/issues/496#issuecomment-1785946907_

title: A possible switch to tidyeval for `values` and `left`/`right` arguments
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **pointblank**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

Currently, the `value` (and `left`/`right`) argument in column comparison validation functions uses `vars()` to resolve scope ambiguity - values passed to `value` are evaluated ordinarily _unless_ protected by `vars()`, in which case it's resolved to a column vector instead.

I think this makes it a prime candidate for integrating **tidyeval**, which resolves this same scope ambiguity with `.data` and `.env`.

### Pros

- We can start the deprecation of `vars(col)` syntax, encouraging users to instead use the `.data$col` pronoun instead.
- Defusing a string variable to select a column is now more straightforward: `vars(!!col_chr)` becomes `.data[[col_chr]]`
- Allows building up more complex expressions like `value = .data$value * .env$multiplier`
- Allows tidyselect via the [bridge pattern](https://rlang.r-lib.org/reference/topic-metaprogramming.html#bridge-patterns) using `pick()`, like `value = pick(any_of("a", "z"))`

Perhaps the biggest PRO of all, this is the familiar and idiomatic dplyr way to do column comparisons dynamically. For example, the `col_vals_gt()`-equivalent logic expressed inside `dplyr::filter()` would look like the following:

``` r
library(dplyr)
b <- 0
df <- tibble(a = 1:2, b = 1)

# data scoping
df %>% 
  filter(a > .data$b)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>       a     b
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1     2     1

# env scoping
df %>% 
  filter(a > .env$b)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>       a     b
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1     1     1
#> 2     2     1

# tidyselect bridge pattern with `pick()` + simplify to vector with `pull()`
df %>% 
  filter(a > pull(pick(any_of(c("b", "z")))))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>       a     b
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1     2     1
```

### Cons

1) The biggest hurdle for a tidyeval implementation is that the current masking pattern in `value` is the **other way around** compared to in tidyeval: the _environment_ masks the _data_. This makes it difficult to recycle the existing infrastructure for tidyeval.

    Instead, this might require implementing our own "poorman's tidyeval". I've attached code for a toy implementation at the end. It's probably not super ideal to introduce a lot of metaprogramming shenanigans, so I'm also very open to simplifying this (ex: we don't _have_ to support bridge pattern with `pick()`).

2) The fact that `vars("x")` gets deprecated in favor of `.data$x` (or `.data[["x"]]`) in `value` may be confusing when combined with (#493), because in the context of tidyselect, `vars("x")` would get deprecated in favor of `all_of("x")` in `columns`. One solution is to not necessarily signal the deprecation of `vars(x)` as used in the `values` argument - we can simply *document* the possibility of passing more complex expressions to `value` by using the `.data` and `.env` pronouns and leave it for the advanced users to discover for themselves.

3) This may pose some limitations for the yaml round-trip. I don't know to what extent there exists a "pointblank guarantee" for this, but we can always be stricter about the input.

## Proposed behavior:

```r
b <- 0
col_b <- "b"
df <- data.frame(a = 1:2, b = 1)

# backwards compatibility
df$a > values_tidyeval(b, df)
#> [1] TRUE TRUE
df$a > values_tidyeval(vars(b), df)
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE
df$a > values_tidyeval(vars("b"), df)
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE
df$a > values_tidyeval(vars(!!col_b), df)
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE

# new pattern for resolving scope ambiguity
df$a > values_tidyeval(.env$b, df) # or just `b`
#> [1] TRUE TRUE
df$a > values_tidyeval(.data$b, df)
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE

library(tidyselect)
# tidyselect variants for selecting the column "b"
df$a > values_tidyeval(pick(all_of("b")), df)
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE
df$a > values_tidyeval(pick(all_of(col_b)), df)
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE
# tidyselect extras
df$a > values_tidyeval(pick(any_of(c("b", "z"))), df)
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE
df$a > values_tidyeval(pick(2), df)
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE

```

<details>
<summary>Mockup implementation of `values_tidyeval()` (with messages for debugging)</summary>

```r
# `vars(col)` and `vars("col")` translated to `.data$col`
vars_as_dotdata <- function(col, ...) {
  rlang::check_dots_empty0()
  col_sym <- rlang::ensym(col)
  eval_expr <- rlang::data_sym(col_sym)
  message("Translated:  ", deparse(eval_expr))
  eval.parent(eval_expr)
}

# tidyselect bridge pattern support
pick_pull <- function(col) {
  data_cols <- eval.parent(quote(names(.data)))
  col_chr <- rlang::inject(tidyselect::vars_pull(data_cols, {{ col }}))
  eval_expr <- rlang::data_sym(col_chr)
  message("Translated:  ", deparse(eval_expr))
  eval.parent(eval_expr)
}

values_tidyeval <- function(x, tbl) {
  x_quo <- rlang::enquo(x)
  message("Received:    ", rlang::expr_deparse(rlang::quo_get_expr(x_quo)))
  if (!rlang::quo_is_call(x_quo)) {
    # Bare symbols and constants are evaluated in the env they come from
    rlang::eval_tidy(x_quo)
  } else {
    # If value is complex expression, evaluate in a "tidyeval" context
    ## 1) Extract expression and environment from quosure
    x_expr <- rlang::quo_get_expr(x_quo)
    x_env <- rlang::quo_get_env(x_quo)
    ## 2) Create a masking environment and introduce pronouns
    x_masked_env <- rlang::new_environment(
      data = list(.data = tbl, .env = x_env),
      parent = x_env
    )
    ## 3) Replace `vars()` and `pick()` with custom implementation
    ##    - inner substitute to mask vars/pick
    ##    - outer substitute to unquote x_expr
    eval_expr <- eval(substitute(substitute(
      x_expr,
      list(vars = quote(vars_as_dotdata), pick = quote(pick_pull))
    )))
    message("Substituted: ", deparse(eval_expr))
    eval(eval_expr, x_masked_env)
  }
}
```
</details>


### Edit: recycling `eval_tidy()`

Just for completeness, it turns out that it *is* also possible to simply swap the data and env roles and still use `eval_tidy()`. But this is purely an implementational issue that can be decided on later.

<details>
<summary>Mockup implementation of `reverse_tidyeval()` that still uses `rlang::eval_tidy()`</summary>

```r
reverse_tidyeval <- function(x, tbl = head(mtcars)) {
  # 1) Capture expression as quosure
  x_quo <- rlang::enquo(x)
  # 2) Extract quosure components
  x_expr <- rlang::quo_get_expr(x_quo)
  x_env <- rlang::quo_get_env(x_quo)
  # 3) Reverse `.data` and `.env` in expression
  x_expr_reversed <- eval(substitute(substitute(
    x_expr, rlang::exprs(.data = .env, .env = .data)
  )))
  # 4) Reverse data and env roles
  data_as_env <- rlang::new_environment(data = tbl)
  ## env-as-data only grabs the variables used in expression
  env_as_data <- rlang::env_get_list(
    x_env, nms = all.names(x_expr, unique = TRUE),
    default = NULL, inherit = TRUE
  )
  # 5) Eval
  rlang::eval_tidy(x_expr_reversed, env_as_data, data_as_env)
}

# New .data syntax for vars()
reverse_tidyeval(.data$mpg)
#> [1] 21.0 21.0 22.8 21.4 18.7 18.1
hp <- 0
# Default is environment scoping
reverse_tidyeval(.data$mpg * hp)
#> [1] 0 0 0 0 0 0
# .env pronoun makes this explicit
reverse_tidyeval(.data$mpg * .env$hp)
#> [1] 0 0 0 0 0 0
# .data to scope in data
reverse_tidyeval(.data$mpg * .data$hp)
#> [1] 2310.0 2310.0 2120.4 2354.0 3272.5 1900.5
# bang-bang to inline values defined in a different scope
local({
  hp <- -1
  reverse_tidyeval(.data$mpg * !!hp)
})
#> [1] -21.0 -21.0 -22.8 -21.4 -18.7 -18.1
```
</details>

title: Integrate `scan_data()` elements into validation reports
description:
I recently attended a workshop where the functionalities of this package were discussed. One question that came up was whether elements from scan_data, such as the map of missing data, could be integrated into the final validation reports. Currently, this feature is not available, but I believe it would add considerable value to the reporting workflow.

Motivation:
The scan_data function provides a comprehensive overview of the data, offering insights into various aspects like variable statistics, interactions, correlations, and missing values. Integrating some of this rich contextual information into the final validation report would make the report much more informative. Users would benefit from having a single, consolidated document that provides both validation results and data quality metrics.

Suggested Implementation:
I envision an optional parameter within the validation function report where users could specify which sections of the scan_data report they want to include in the final validation report. For instance:

```r
agent_3 %>% 
  get_agent_report(include_scan_data_sections = c("O", "M"))  # Include 'Overview' and 'Missing Values' from scan_data
)
```

This approach would give users the flexibility to choose what additional information they find relevant for their specific use case.

title: Integrate with pins for writing agents, informants
description:
Object ops functions for agents and informants revolve around writing and reading from disk.  

A logical workflow would include writing agents and informants to a pin with a board back end on Connect, S3, or other. 

This would enable reading agents or informants into downstream reports or apps.  Notably, creation of multiagents would be significantly improved if the multiagent could be created from a versioned pin. 

One current challenge with trying to do this manually is the size of the agent object when written. The input `tbl` is redundantly saved within each validation. This makes the object very large difficult to pin. Some optimization in the agent object would be required. Then this would be a super slick workflow.

title: `get_agent_x_list()$columns` is empty for `col_vals_expr()`
description:
I notice that, for col_vals_expr(), the `columns` slot of the object returned by `get_agent_x_list()` is NA.
This is linked to https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues/475, but as a slightly broader issue (such as "For failed rows, access columns used in validation, and only those").

In my code in issue https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues/475, instead of
`columns_to_display <- unique c((id_columns, get_agent_x_list(agent, i = c_step)$columns ))`
I use the following workaround, with a hack involving `all.vars(as.formula())`:

 ```
c_agent_step <- get_agent_x_list(agent, i = c_rule)
 if (c_agent_step$type == "col_vals_expr") {
    columns_to_display <- unique (c(id_columns,
                                    # get the variables from the expr-ession used in col_vals_expr()
                                    all.vars(as.formula( paste0("~", c_agent_step$values)))) )
  } else {
    columns_to_display <- unique (c(id_columns, c_agent_step$columns) )
  }
```
My use case here is a validation step involving:
```
  col_vals_expr(
    expr = expr( paste0("some_string", column1) == column2))
```
I would suggest adding something to fill in the  `columns` slot  in such cases (and maybe for `specially()`, too).

title: `get_data_extracts()` gets less data for `rows_distinct()` than for `col_vals_*()⁠`
description:
## Description
get_data_extracts() behaves differently for  validation functions of the form ⁠col_vals_*()⁠, conjointly() and rows_distinct()
For rows_distinct, the tibble contains only the tested columns, contrary to the other functions.


## Reproducible example

```
library(pointblank)
library(dplyr)

tbl <- tibble(id1=1:5,
                     id2=c("A", "b", "C", "D", "E"),
                     a = c(8, 8, 8, 5, 9),
                     b = c(11,11:14),
                     date = as.Date(paste0("2023-01-0",1:5)))

# The columns or set of columns that need to be displayed
# (to help identify the row) along the column with invalid value
id_columns <- c("id1", "id2")

agent <-
  create_agent(
    tbl = tbl,
    tbl_name = "small_table",
    label = "An example."
  ) %>%
  col_vals_gt(columns = vars(a), value = 6) %>%
  col_vals_gt(columns = vars(b), value = 11) %>%
  col_vals_regex(columns = vars(id2), regex = "[A-Z]")   %>%
  rows_distinct(columns = vars(a))  %>%
  rows_distinct(columns = c("b"))  %>%
  rows_distinct(columns = c("a", "b"))  %>%
  conjointly(
    ~ col_vals_lt(., columns = vars(a), value = 7),
    ~ col_vals_gt(., columns = vars(a), value = vars(b)))   %>%
  col_is_date(columns =  "date") %>%
  interrogate()

agent

agent %>% get_agent_report(display_table = FALSE)

# Loop over each step and display a selection of columns from failing rows
for (c_step in 1:nrow(get_agent_report(agent, display_table = F))){
  print("====================")
  get_agent_x_list(agent, i = c_step)$briefs %>% print
  print(c("current step: ", c_step))
  get_agent_x_list(agent, i = c_step)$columns %>% print
  columns_to_display <- unique c((id_columns, get_agent_x_list(agent, i = c_step)$columns ))
  get_data_extracts(agent, i=c_step)  %>%
    select(columns_to_display)  %>%  # comment this line out to see the result
    print
}

```
## Expected result
For the col_vals_*()⁠ and conjointly() function, get_data_extracts() returns all columns, which allows further selection of the columns one wishes to keep for display.
However, for `rows_distinct(columns=vars(a))`, only the 'a' column remains. I do not know of a way to get the full rows for the failing rows with pointblank.
Using  `agent %>% get_agent_report(display_table = TRUE)`, the same issue holds for the "CSV" buttons.

In the example, we want two columns, id1 and id2, to be displayed (to help identify the failing row) along with the column with invalid values.
Commenting out the following line in the code above helps see the difference in behaviour:

title: Unexpected behavior from `get_tbl_information_dbi` when `tbl` name created with `dbplyr::in_schema`
description:
The code found [here](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/d92d7e24d88116aa4adc709ef5da862a38aa3ac2/R/utils.R#L816) produces behavior which will cause failure, including of core functions like `create_agent`

If the tbl supplied to `create_agent` is created with `dbplyr::in_schema` like so:
```{r}
con <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())
test_tbl <- tbl(con, dbplyr::in_schema(schema = "public", table = "<table_name>"))
```

Then, `get_tbl_information_dbi` will convert the table name into a length two character vector. Then when the `q_types` query is created it will also be a length two character vector. When the query is sent to the db, it fails.

@rich-iannone, I would love any guidance on how to create a reprex for these types of issues. I have needed to create them for other bugs I've found in R packages, but haven't been able to figure out how to mock the db connection.

Anyways, I'm happy to take a swing at fixing this. I'm thinking we could check the class of `dbplyr::remote_name(tbl)` and change behavior accordingly. Thoughts or alternatives?

## Proposal

We've configured our Workbench to use an ODBC connection which means that the database details are configured on the system and the user really just needs to provide their username and pw credentials to connect to a database. When connecting, a `con` object is created. For those that are interested in using pointblank for accessing remote databases, it would be nice if the `con` object could be used in `db_tbl` rather than have to specify all the database properties.

db_tbl(con, table = "schema.table", ...)
```

## Description

The `get_agent_report(agent, title = "a custom title", size = "small)` does not change the default title of the table.

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(pointblank)
tbl <- dplyr::tibble(a = c(5, 7, 8, 5))
agent <-
  create_agent(
    tbl = tbl,
    tbl_name = "small_table",
    label = "An example."
  ) %>%
  col_vals_gt(columns = vars(a), value = 4) %>%
  interrogate()

get_agent_report(
  agent = agent,
  title = "a custom title",
  size = "small"
)

get_agent_report(
  agent = agent,
  title = "a custom title",
  size = "standard"
)
```

In this example, both the standard and small tables should have the title "a custom title".

title: Improve speed of `rows_distinct()` on large databases
description:
I have been testing pointblank on a very large RSQLite database with more than 2 billion rows.
While most build-in validation functions were running quite fast, the validation of `rows_dinstinct()` took about 3.5 hours for 480M rows table. It was crashing on larger tables.
So I was checking if this was generally due to SQL DISTINCT being slow, but could find that this only took 22 minutes on the same data.

I could not detect in the code what makes `rows_distinct()` so extremely slow (possibly pre-/post processing?), but honestly I couldn't even see whether the code uses `dplyr::distinct()` or dbplyr translations for databases.

To test, I have added a benchmark example below. Be careful, it uses about 500 MB of temp local storage and 5-10 minutes to run the benchmarks.

```

```

Results are

- that SQL distinct is a bit difficult to compare, but with adding another count to materialize results, without that I always get a few milliseconds independent of number of rows
- `dplyr::distinct()` on a tibble takes max 1.5 second to run
- `pointblank::rows_distinct()` however needs almost a minute to run (factor 30-40 slower than dplyr and at least factor 10 slower than SQL distinct).
- no notable difference in pointblank timings between tibbles and SQL tables


``` r
library(pointblank)
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
#> Warning: package 'RSQLite' was built under R version 4.2.2
library(tidyverse)
#> Warning: package 'ggplot2' was built under R version 4.2.2
#> Warning: package 'stringr' was built under R version 4.2.2
library(bench)

#create large synth data
n_pat    <- 1E6
n_diag   <- 1E7

diag <- tibble(
  repid   = sample(1:n_pat, size = n_diag, replace = TRUE), 
  abrq    = sample(20101:20224, size = n_diag, replace = TRUE),
  icd     = sample(c("E01, E02, E11, E12"), size = n_diag, replace = TRUE),
  icd_sub = paste0(icd, ".9")
) %>%
  arrange(repid)

#connect sql db
sql_loc <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), dbname = tempfile())
dbWriteTable(sql_loc, "diag", diag)

#benchmark pointblank::rows_distinct vs. dplyr::distinct 
#added another count to make sure that SQL DISTINCT is actually materialized

results <- 
  bench::press(
    rows = c(1E4, 1E5, 1E6, 1E7),
    bench::mark(
      pointblank_distinct_sql = create_agent(
        tbl = {tbl(sql_loc, "diag") %>% head(rows)}) %>%
        rows_distinct() %>% 
        interrogate(extract_failed = FALSE),
      pointblank_distinct_tib = create_agent(
        tbl = {tbl(sql_loc, "diag") %>% head(rows)}) %>%
        rows_distinct() %>% 
        interrogate(extract_failed = FALSE),
      dplyr_distinct_sql = tbl(sql_loc, "diag") %>%
        head(n = rows) %>%
        distinct() %>%
        tally() %>%
        collect(),
      dplyr_distinct_tib = diag %>%
        head(n = rows) %>%
        distinct() %>%
        tally(),
      check = FALSE,
      iterations = 2
    )
  )

title: error \uxxxx sequences not supported inside backticks
description:
## Description

When running code with emojis inside backticks (as shown in the info_tabular function below, I get the following error: "error \uxxxx sequences not supported inside backticks".  Interestingly, the emoji works in other sections when not surrounded by backticks as shown in the "label" argument of the code below.  

UPDATE: The following code works when running on a Mac so appears to be something with Windows.  Any idea why it wouldn't run in Windows?  

## Reproducible example

```
informant_pp <- 
  create_informant(
    tbl = ~ palmerpenguins::penguins,
    label = "The dataset from the **palmerpenguins** 🔄."
  ) %>% 
  info_tabular(`🔄 updates` = "🔄 This table is not regularly updated.")

informant_pp

```
## Expected result

To have the emoji display in info_tabular section when I print informant_pp; instead I get the following error: Error: \uxxxx sequences not supported inside backticks (line 7). 

## Session info

R version 4.1.3 (2022-03-10)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 10 x64 (build 19044)

Thanks in advance, great work on development of pointblank, really useful!  Let me know if any other info needed.  Bill

The 'export_report()' function fails when trying to write an .html report for a multiagent object. It fails with `object 'object_type' not found` without a trace to where the error had happened.

``` r
#reprex.pointblank.export.multiagent.R

  rows_distinct() %>% 
  interrogate()

agent2 <- create_agent(tbl = game_revenue) %>% 
  rows_distinct() %>% 
  interrogate()

multiagent <- create_multiagent(agent1,
                                agent2)

export_report(multiagent, 
              filename = "report.html")
#> Error in eval(parse(text = text, keep.source = FALSE), envir): object 'object_type' not found

## Description

I'm not 100% sure this is a pointblank bug and not a quarto bug, but starting here.

In a quarto project with `execute-dir: project`, interrogation tables in .qmd files not in the root directory cause the following error on render:

```
Quitting from lines 6-20 (test.qmd) 
Error in readLines(con, warn = FALSE) : cannot open the connection
Calls: .main ... <Anonymous> -> enumerate_output_formats -> read_utf8 -> readLines

If I do any of the following, the error goes away and the .qmd renders correctly:
- Move test.qmd to the project root directory
- Remove `execute-dir: project` from _quarto.yml
- use `quarto::quarto_render("dir/test.qmd", execute_dir = "dir")` to override the execute-dir YAML setting

## Reproducible example

Reprex here: https://github.com/Aariq/pointblank-debug. Open dir/test.qmd and click "render"

I wouldn't expect `pointblank` to care about the execute-dir.

title: Wrong column types variable with DuckDB
description:
See https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/discussions/445

Let's create a smaller reproducible error:

```
# WITH THE PACKAGE PROJECT OPEN!

devtools::load_all()
library(dplyr)
library(duckdb)

dout <- tempdir()

readr::write_csv(mtcars, paste0(dout, "/mtcars.csv"))

con_mem <- dbConnect(duckdb(), dbdir = ":memory:", read_only = FALSE)

duckdb_read_csv(con_mem, name = "mtcars", files = paste0(dout, "/mtcars.csv"))

scan_data(tbl(con_mem, "mtcars")) # FAILS

── Data Scan started. Processing 6 sections. ────────────────────────────────────────────────
ℹ Starting assembly of 'Overview' section...
Error in `dplyr::pull()`:
! Can't extract columns that don't exist.
✖ Column `DATA_TYPE` doesn't exist.
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
```

Let's look at the details by using rlang
```
> rlang::last_error()
<error/vctrs_error_subscript_oob>
Error in `dplyr::pull()`:
! Can't extract columns that don't exist.
✖ Column `DATA_TYPE` doesn't exist.
---
Backtrace:
  1. pointblank::scan_data(tbl(con_mem, "mtcars"))
 13. dplyr:::pull.data.frame(., ifelse(tbl_src == "bigquery", "data_type", "DATA_TYPE"))
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see the full context.
```

The conflict seems to be here: https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/main/R/utils.R#L813

If we use the PostgreSQL connection from the link above, we get
```
>  get_tbl_dbi_src_details(tbl)
[1] "postgres  [teacher@databases.pacha.dev:5432/intendo]

> gsub("^([a-z]*).*", "\\1", get_tbl_dbi_src_details(tbl))
[1] "postgres"
```

With the duckdb connection we have
```
> get_tbl_dbi_src_details(tbl)
[1] "DuckDB 0.5.1 [pacha@Linux 5.14.0-1054-oem:R 4.2.1/:memory:]"
> gsub("^([a-z]*).*", "\\1", get_tbl_dbi_src_details(tbl))
[1] ""
```

A simple change to `gsub("^([a-z]*).*|", "\\1", tolower(get_tbl_dbi_src_details(tbl)))` is sufficient. I sent a PR.

If an Rmd chunk with `validate = TRUE` ends with a non-printing statement, the entire file fails to knit. A conceivable example of this would be a comment. ## Reproducible example Using the [template Rmd](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/main/inst/rmarkdown/templates/pointblank-validation/skeleton/skeleton.Rmd) and adding additional content that produces no printed output (e.g. assignment or a comment) at the end of the chunk, e.g. ```` ```{r validation_step_functions, validate = TRUE} col_exists(small_table, columns = vars(a, b, c, d, e, f)) rows_distinct(small_table, vars(d, e)) col_vals_gt(small_table, vars(d), 1000) # this shouldn't matter ``` ```` Less likely to occur, but not (as far as I could see) advised against: ```` ```{r validation_step_functions, validate = TRUE} col_exists(small_table, columns = vars(a, b, c, d, e, f)) rows_distinct(small_table, vars(d, e)) col_vals_gt(small_table, vars(d), 1000) a <- 1 ``` ```` Non-printing statements elsewhere in the chunk appear to work fine. Similarly for the (usually passing) piped example ```` ```{r validate = TRUE} small_table %>% col_is_date("date") %>% col_vals_gt(vars(d), vars(c), na_pass = TRUE) # ``` ```` or ```` ```{r validate = TRUE} small_table %>% col_is_date("date") %>% col_vals_gt(vars(d), vars(c), na_pass = TRUE) %>% invisible() ``` ```` When ending with a non-printing statement, the file fails to knit with error: ``` Error in if (agent_tbl_vec[i]) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed Calls: ... block_exec -> eng_r -> -> remix_content Execution halted ``` I can only guess, but perhaps something to do with `extract_output()`. I did note the advice > For best rendering results, don't place anything else inside the chunk but I took that to mean it was optional - it appears it's essential that the final statement produces some output. Statements on the final line that output something appear to be okay ```` ```{r validation_step_functions, validate = TRUE} col_exists(small_table, columns = vars(a, b, c, d, e, f)) rows_distinct(small_table, vars(d, e)) col_vals_gt(small_table, vars(d), 1000) 1 ``` ```` or with `identity(1)`, `1+1`, or `(a <- 1)`, but not `invisible(1)` or `stopifnot(TRUE)`. ## Expected result No errors should be produced, the file should knit as usual. ## Session info

title: actions_levels and all_passed question
description:
## Description

So I'm using pointblank in the context of shiny, and as far as I understand (please correct me if I'm wrong !), `all_passed` is the only way to get the result of an interrogation.
Although I'm setting specific `action_levels` to not trigger any of these, the test is still failing with `col_vals_not_null` since there are some NA values, which is ok up to a point that I thought I could define with the `action_levels`. 

## Reproducible example
This will return FALSE.
```
a <- dplyr::tibble(
    a = c(5, 7, 6, 5, NA, 7)
) %>%
    create_agent(
        label = "A very *simple* example.",
        actions = action_levels(notify_at = 0.9, warn_at = 0.95, stop_at = 0.99)
    ) %>%
col_vals_not_null(vars(a)) %>% 
    interrogate()

all_passed(a)
```
## Expected result

Not sure, but at first I thought that this would pass.

## Question
I have a lot of integer values, not in a specific set, and there can be NAs in there as well. How can I check that I don't have more than 10% for instance, without failing the test, e.g. 9% of NAs would be OK.

Apologies of I missunderstood how this all works. Hopefully someone will be able to shed some light on this :)

  rows_complete(vars(a))

  rows_complete(c(a))

title: Scoping issue in col_vals_expr()
description:
## Description

I sometimes use `col_vals_expr()` to attach a check to an agent that is not directly related to the data that is being checked. When I do this inside a function it does throw an evaluation error because, apparently, the variables used in the expression are searched for in the global environment rather than the function environment.

## Reproducible example

```
tbl <-
  dplyr::tibble(
    a = c(1, 2, 1, 7, 8, 6),

title: pointblank throws error on grouped dataset
description:
## Description

I accidently passed a grouped dataset to a pointblank agent and had to spend some time on finding out what caused the error. If throwing an error is intended behaviour in this situation it would be nice to have a self-explaining error message.

## Reproducible example

```
small_table |> 
  group_by(e) |> 
  create_agent() |> 
  col_vals_in_set(vars(a, c), 1:10) |> 
  interrogate()
```

## Session info

Tested on pointblank 0.10.0

title: Add `Details` section to agent report for additional reporting artifacts
description:
While each line in the agent report provides a succinct summary of a validation step (before and after interrogation), it’s hard to gain additional insight without immediately looking into the agent object.

it would be great to have more information available within a `Details` section inside the footer. In this way, we can make intel files available for the entire interrogation.

title: Display a validation coverage schematic
description: It would be great to have displayed (at the bottom of the validation report) a schematic that visualizes the validation coverage. This should give a rough indication on which columns have been validated, whether whole rows were validated, whether the schema was validated, all that. If a numeric metric could be generated along with this (and it feels right), that would also be a plus.

title: Add the `col_count_match()` function
description: The new `col_count_match()` function should be added, with an interface the parallels the `row_count_match()` function with the proposed changes described in https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues/395.

title: Allow for literal row count as input for `row_count_match()`
description: The `row_count_match()` function should flexibly allow for either a secondary table as input for comparison (as it is currently) *or* a literal numeric value. The `tbl_compare` argument should be renamed as `count`.

title: Provide syntax for table store to extend table-prep from previous formulas
description:
The table store is a nice way to obtain tables from disparate locations and define preparations for alternate views. It could however be redundant to obtain a table as `tbl_main` in one incantation, and then repeat the logic and more transformation steps in a supposed `tbl_main_recent`. Something better might be this:

```r
tbl_store(
  tbl_main ~ get(tbl_main),
  tbl_main_recent ~ {{ tbl_main }} %>% < additional transformation steps >
)
```

To avoid too much unneeded complexity perhaps the rule could be that references to identifiers must be limited to those previously defined. This could enforce an ordering of table preparations that would only increase in the number of dependencies (i.e., tables needed to produce other tables).

title: Create a compatibility table that shows which table types (local and database) work with which validation functions
description: Given the large amount of data sources that **pointblank** supports, it would be useful to have a table that compares which validation functions are verified to work across the different sources. It's also important to ensure that this table is updated consistently and that it's based on frequently running tests across the different backends.

title: Allow for more width options for the informant report
description: Currently, the default width of the informant report is `"standard"` (and there is a `"small"` option, which also inlines CSS for better emailing) but this makes reading of the report a bit uncomfortable in many situations. What should be allowed are user-specified widths in both `%` and `px`. The `"small"` keyword should probably be removed in favor of a separate option for creating an email-able version.

title: typo in soft deprecation warning when using read_fn
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.
* [ ] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
    * [ ] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [ ] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [ ] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

## Description

The warning issued when using `read_fn` reads:

```r
Warning message:
The `read_fn` argument is undergoing soft deprecation; instead:
 * Use the in the `tbl` argument for in-memory tables.
 * Or supply a function or table-prep formula to `tbl`. 
 ```
There is a _the in_ to much in the first bullet.

Sorry, but I don't have the time right now to open af PR to fix this, so this will have to do (for now at least)

Best
Lars

title: Optionally store information on user environment during interrogation
description: For keeping track of reproducibility, it might be useful to capture and store which pointblank version was used during interrogation. The dependencies should also be stored. Besides having this information on hand should anyone need it, it might also be useful to warn the user (optionally) if a very old version of pointblank and important dependencies are being used.

title: Remove the `read_fn` arg and make a more useful `tbl` arg
description: Some functions have a `tbl` arg (to read in a table immediately) and a `read_fn` arg (to read in a table lazily with a function or formula). I think this is confusing and could be simplified with a `tbl` arg that handles both eager and lazy table reading.

title: Add a function to stop interrogation process if condition is met
description: It would be useful to have a function that (nicely) breaks the interrogation process if some condition is met. It should be able to draw on intel for the current step and collection of all steps processed. The reporting should clearly show the reason for the stoppage in the reporting and the show which steps were not processed.

title: Add the `tbl_match()` function for cell-by-cell comparison between tables
description:
There are some cases where you'd want to check whether two instances of a table are exactly the same (same schema, same row counts, same values in each corresponding cell). Perhaps to experiment with two methods of transforming a table and other reasons I'm sure.

For such cases, the `tbl_match()` function (and corresponding expectation/test variants) is needed. The groundwork for this was prepared by having the `row_count_match()` function and the earlier `col_schema_match()` function. The cell-by-cell checking should be handled by internal use of `test_col_vals_equal()`. It's important that this should work reasonably well when tables are from different sources (e.g., one in DB, one local or different DB). There should also be affordances to loosen the strictness of this checking (as there is in `col_schema_match()`). Finally, the reporting associated with an agent-based step of this nature should be adequate enough such that failures can be easily zeroed-in on.

title: Add the `row_count_match()` function
description:
We need a validation function that determines whether two tables have the same row count. Importantly, it should not matter where these tables are located (e.g., one might be a data frame, the other a DB table; we might have two tables in different databases).

Also important: need to support laziness in accessing the comparison table (this is something the `col_schema()` function, which can also use an external table, does not yet support).

title: `incorporate()` fails with multi-element fields in `info_tabular()`
description:
## Description

When `info_tabular()` is provided a multi-element argument to one of its dots parameters, `incorporate()` fails with error `All unnamed arguments must be length 1`.

Without running `incorporate()`, the processing succeeds and the multi-element input is nicely turned into multiple lines in the output.

This can be worked around but the multi-element input is a succinct way of creating multi-line description fields, also making the source code more legible.

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(pointblank)

# bug

x <- create_informant(tbl = mtcars,
                 label = "Codebook") %>%
  info_tabular(Info = c("Line 1",
                        "Line 2"),
               `Additional` = "Extra info") %>%
  
  info_snippet(
    snippet_name = "min_wt",
    fn = snip_lowest(column = "wt")
  ) %>%
  info_columns("wt",
               Popis = "weight",
               Min = "minimum is {min_wt}") %>%
  incorporate()
```

    #> 

    #> ── Incorporation Started - there is a single snippet to process ────────────────

    #> ✓ Information gathered.

    #> ✓ Snippets processed.

    #> Error: All unnamed arguments must be length 1

``` r
# snippet and incorporate, single-element info

x <- create_informant(tbl = mtcars,
                 label = "Codebook") %>%
  info_tabular(Info = c("Line 1"),
               `Additional` = "Extra info") %>%
  info_snippet(
    snippet_name = "min_wt",
    fn = snip_lowest(column = "wt")
  ) %>%
  info_columns("wt",
               Popis = "weight",
               Min = "minimum is {min_wt}") %>%
  incorporate()
```

    #> 

    #> ── Incorporation Started - there is a single snippet to process ────────────────

    #> ✓ Information gathered.

    #> ✓ Snippets processed.

    #> ✓ Information built.

    #> 

    #> ── Incorporation Completed ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

``` r
# no snippet, no incorporate

x <- create_informant(tbl = mtcars,
                 label = "Codebook") %>%
  info_tabular(Info = c("Line 1",
                        "Line 2"),
               `Additional` = "Extra info") %>%
  info_columns("wt",
               Popis = "weight")

# no snippet, incorporate, two-element info

x <- create_informant(tbl = mtcars,
                 label = "Codebook") %>%
  info_tabular(Info = c("Line 1",
                        "Line 2"),
               `Additional` = "Extra info") %>%
  info_columns("wt",
               Popis = "weight") %>% 
  incorporate()
```

    #> 

    #> ── Incorporation Started ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    #> ✓ Information gathered.

    #> Error: All unnamed arguments must be length 1

<sup>Created on 2021-11-24 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

## Expected result

I would expect the pipeline to handle multi-element input identically regardless of whether snippets and `incorporate()` are part of the flow

title: `yaml_write()` fails when `active` argument is a function that returns FALSE
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.
* [x] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
    * [ ] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [ ] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [ ] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

## Description

The `yaml_write()` function does not appear to work when `active` is provided an anonymous function the returns `FALSE`. 

I suspect #345 could be related since it covers another edge case where `write_yaml()` fails a receiving a function versus a value as input. However, I thought this seemed like a distinct enough problem to merit its own issue.

The broader context for this problem is:

- I want to have checks in my pipeline that may not have matches (e.g. `starts_with('N')` when data may or may not have any such columns) 
- In `pointblank` 0.6.0, I was able to do this so long as I explicitly provided the `step_id`
- I find in `pointblank` 0.8.0 and beyond, I get errors unless I use the `active` argument (shown in first part of reprex)
- Passing a function to `active` makes interrogation work but breaks `write_yaml()` if the function returns `FALSE` 

## Reproducible example

* [x] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
    * [ ] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [ ] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [ ] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

``` r
library(pointblank)

# no `active` doesn't interrogate ----
agent1 <-
  create_agent(read_fn = ~data.frame(IND_A = 1, AMT_B = 2)) %>%
  col_vals_not_null(starts_with("ID"), step_id = 1) %>%
  col_vals_not_null(starts_with("IND"), step_id = 2)

res1 <- interrogate(agent1)
```

    #> Error: Only strings can be converted to symbols

``` r
# `active` (FALSE function) does interrogate; doesn't write yaml ----
agent2 <-
  create_agent(read_fn = ~data.frame(IND_A = 1, AMT_B = 2)) %>%
  col_vals_not_null(
    starts_with("ID"), step_id = 1,
    active = ~. %>% {length(starts_with("ID", vars = colnames(.))) > 0} ) %>%
  col_vals_not_null(starts_with("IND"), step_id = 2)

res2 <- interrogate(agent2)
```

    #> i Step 1 is not set as active. Skipping.

``` r
yaml_write(agent2, filename = "pb-test-2.yml", path = tempdir())
```

``` r
# `active` (TRUE function) does interrogate; writes yaml ----
agent3 <-
  create_agent(read_fn = ~data.frame(IND_A = 1, AMT_B = 2)) %>%
  col_vals_not_null(
    starts_with("AMT"), step_id = 1,
    active = ~. %>% {length(starts_with("AMT", vars = colnames(.))) > 0} ) %>%

title: Beyond data frames?
description:
Hi, authors! 

I came here via Emily's [post](https://emilyriederer.netlify.app/post/data-valid-lightweight/) This seems like a very elaborate and carefully designed framework. Good job!

Not all data lives in a data frame. It may be valuable to make it convenient to create custom expectations to allow the user to take advantage of the very nice reporting utilities.  For example, I may want to check how many of my API returns are valid, or what portion of my logs match a certain regex pattern. 

Is it within scope to generalize and extend the domain of this package to any R objects?

title: Introduce the `gauntlet()` function, for validation
description:
We really need the `gauntlet()` function for gauntlet-style validations. This can sometimes be useful should you want to do some test checks in a sequence but if a prior step doesn’t work out, don’t proceed to the next steps. It’s basically putting your validations in a gauntlet.

A use case: check a column type, perform a validation on the same column based on the same column type. (You wouldn’t do validation 2 if validation 1 didn’t check out.)

Another one: create a series of steps that checks whether two tables are the same. You might first check whether the schemas match, then, see if the row counts match, then check whether the byte sizes match, then, finally, do column-by-column checks of the cell values. By running the checks through a gauntlet, we could get an informative error at the point of failure (i.e., if the tables didn’t match).

  info_columns(matches("mpg"), info = "there")
yaml_write(a)

## Description

In an informant workflow, when the selector in `info_columns()` does not match any columns:

- an `NA` column is reported in the output if the `info_columns()` call is at the end of the pipeline (Example 2 below)

``` r
library(pointblank)

mtcars %>% 
  create_informant() %>% 
  info_columns(matches("x"), info = "hi") %>%

For both scenarios, I would expect a warning or message and for the output to be unaffected by any `info_columns()` whose selectors match no columns. Alternatively, there might be some way to report in the output the failures to match columns.

title: Have `all_passed()` return FALSE when there are evaluation errors?
description:
I often want `all_passed()` to return FALSE if there is anything other than `TRUE` in the result, e.g. `agent$validation_set$all_passed`. This means, NA would be interpreted as a failure and from what I have gathered, this happens when there is an evaluation error. I can see benefits to both behaviors, current behavior and the one I am suggesting. Maybe it would be worth it to add a parameter like `na_rm` or `evaluation_error` so that users can fine tune what `all_passed()` means. Example below:

```r
library(pointblank)

out <- small_table %>% 
  create_agent(actions = action_levels(
    warn_at = 0.2,
    stop_at = 0.8,
    notify_at = 0.5
  )) %>%
  col_vals_not_null(vars("z")) %>%  # <-- evaluation error
  col_exists("f") %>% 
  interrogate()

# returns NA but I would prefer it returns FALSE
all_passed(out)

# vector of passed/failed
out$validation_set$all_passed
```

title: Return failure rows in CSV but have `all_passed()` return TRUE
description:
I have the following system in place:
1. I run quality reports daily using `pointblank`
2. For each report, I call `all_passed()` on the agent 
3. If all passes, I store in the report in a specific folder on our server
4. If something fails, I copy the report to the `failure` directory on our server

However, there are some checks that have failures and I want those checks to be ignored when calling `all_passed()`. Additionally, I still want this check to exist so that there is a record of the rows having this quality issue. These are basically errors in the data that for various reasons, will never be fixed but I nonetheless want people to be aware of it.

title: Informant could include figures
description:
Not an issue, but an idea of something to add:

Something that would be really helpful to see in the informant report is a figure showing the distribution of the data.  Like a histogram or density plot.  Maybe you could incorporate some ggpplot2 features?

title: Fail gracefully when calling info_columns when column doesn't exist
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **pointblank**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

It would be nice to have the `active` parameter in `info_columns()` so that it no longer fails when trying to document a missing column. Here is a small example that explains the problem, what the potential feature might look like, and what I am doing now in the mean time:

```r
library(pointblank)

# this issue
small_table %>% 
  info_columns(
    column = "j",
    info = "foo bar"
  )

# potential feature, add agent semantics to informant
small_table %>% 
  info_columns(
    column = vars("j"),
    info = "foo bar",
    active = ~ . %>% has_columns(vars(j))
  )

# what i am doing now
small_table %>%
  tryCatch(
    expr = {
      info_columns(
        column = "j",
        info = "foo bar"
      )
    }, error = function(e) .
  )
```

title: Add table transformers
description:
Given that we can and should make modifications to the target table (either through table-prep formulas or temporarily in `preconditions` stages), it would be useful to provide a set of table transformers. The idea is to make it much easier to reliably transform the table and perform different types of validations. 

Here are the potential table transformers:

- `tt_summary_stats()` - provide summary statistics for the numerical columns
- `tt_string_info()` - provide basic properties of string-based columns
- `tt_tbl_dims()` - provide rows and column counts 
- `tt_time_shift()` - shift values of date-time column
- `tt_time_slice()` - keep rows above or below a specified time in a date-time column

Function names are tentative.

title: Add the `rows_complete()` validation function
description:
Sometimes you need to check whether rows are complete (i.e., don’t have an `NA`/`NULL` anywhere in the row). This is sorta possible with `conjointly()` and throwing a lot of `col_vals_not_null()` in that, but it’s hella inconvenient. So, `rows_complete()` is the better way.

Sometimes `NULL`s are just fine in certain columns, so, there should be an arg to *exclude* certain columns. I’m hoping excluding rather than including would be the right approach here.

Another scenario is that certain rows needn’t be checked for missing values. I’m hoping that the segmentation feature (recently added in) could handle that nicely.

title: clinically-oriented codeboook/data dictionary
description:
## Proposal

Hi Rich - 
Just a particular viewpoint - it can be really helpful to be able to generate a codebook for clinical data in a semi-automated fashion, a lot like a REDCap codebook [redcap](https://www.iths.org/news/redcap-tip/redcap-tip-of-the-month-leveraging-the-codebook/) This is a bit of a wish list, but here goes:

1. make a tibble that can be exported to things like excel
   a. option to make pretty pdf, HTML, Word Rmd if desired.
2. include columns for 
   a. variable_name
   b. variable_pretty (still short, but with spaces, title case for tables) - may require user to enter if no labels
   c. variable description (long & detailed) - likely to require user to enter
   d. for numeric - mean, median, range
   e. for factors - each level
   f. for all vars - % missing
3. somehow handle labels coming in from SAS, SPSS, Stata
   a. one suggestion - link values to value labels, i.e. values 0-3, with labels "none", "mild", "moderate", "severe", as 0_none, 1_mild, 2_moderate, 3_severe
  b. pull in variable labels - possibly as variable_pretty

Can have more detail - see data dictionary from REDCap
Details on an example of a standard REDCap data dictionary can be found here :  https://www.utsouthwestern.edu/edumedia/edufiles/about_us/admin_offices/academic_information_services/redcap-database-creating-dictionary.pdf

I hope that this is helpful.  Could be a function like 
make_codebook()
or
make_data_dictionary()

title: Tolerance for testing column value equality
description:
Apply this to `col_vals_equal()` and `col_vals_not_equal()` (plus the variants of those functions). Use whatever *testthat* 3e uses for tolerance (based on `all_equal()`). Make sure this works in YAML, when creating testthat files, and across all data sources (e.g., databases). Thank you @eveyp for this! (original post from Discussions below) ### Discussed in https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/discussions/325
Originally posted by **eveyp** June 30, 2021 Would it be possible to specify a tolerance when testing if column values are equal to a specified value? This would be helpful to avoid floating point round off issues. It could be similar to how `testthat` has `expect_equal()` which allows for a tolerance and `expect_identical()` which requires the values to be exactly the same (https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/equality-expectations.html).

title: How to pass variable names to the preconditions argument
description:
I am looking to check the length of strings in a dataset (along the same lines of #140). However, I would like to create a function for this test to reduce repetition in my code (such as when I want to check a large number of variables). 

The roadblock I've run into is that I can't get a variable name I pass to the function I created (`check_length` below) to be used in the `preconditions` argument. In the reprex below, I create two pointblank agents. The first runs successfully, but the second does not because I use the `check_length()` function.

Is there a way to pass a variable name to the preconditions argument or a better way to go about this?

``` r
library(pointblank)
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)

# convert factor columns to character
penguins_char <- penguins %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character))

# function to check the length of a variable
check_length <- function(x, variable, length) {
  x %>%
    col_vals_lte(
      vars(z),
      value = length,
      na_pass = TRUE,
      preconditions = ~ . %>% mutate(z = str_length({{variable}}))
    )
}

# This works
penguins_char %>%
  create_agent(
    actions = action_levels(stop_at = 1)
  ) %>%
  # is the island column <= 6 characters long?
  col_vals_lte(
    vars(z),
    value = 6,
    na_pass = TRUE,
    preconditions = ~ . %>% mutate(z = str_length(island))
  ) %>%
  interrogate()
```

####### REMOVED HTML output

``` r

# This does not work
penguins_char %>%
  create_agent(
    actions = action_levels(stop_at = 1)
  ) %>%
  # is the island column <= 6 characters long?
  check_length(island, 6) %>%
  interrogate()
```

title: Support checks for repeated measures / panel data
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **pointblank**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

I'm opening this issue per our discussion (#297)

When working with panel data, I often find it is helpful to do checks _within_ each observation. For example, if one is analyzing data for a set of customers, it could be useful to specify checks within observations, such as:

- Uniqueness of a column within but not between groups (e.g. YEAR is unique given COUNTRY but different COUNTRYs can have the same YEAR)
- Values increasing within each group (but can decrease between)
- The values of some column within each group contain all values of a prespecified set, so check can fail in all values exist in column but do not exist for each group

Current workarounds include: 

- running `interrogate()` with a nest-map paradigm; however, this seems unnecessarily inefficient and would fragment the out-of-the-box reporting in an awkward way
- sometimes using `preconditions` to create mock columns that can "trick" the checks into working (e.g. hacks like seeing if `account_number * 1000 + other_thing_i_want_to_be_unique_by_group` is unique); however, this doesn't work for all checks (e.g. the "set" checks)

In the discussion thread, we discuss potential solutions such as:

- an optional `groups` argument in the checks
- using `dplyr`-esque check for `groups_vars()` / `groups` aesthetic

Caveats to think about include:

- It's also interesting to think about how this changes reporting. In cases where users are looking for errors within group, I'm not sure if the more useful "success metric" would be the number of "bad" rows or the number of _observations_ that have any bad rows 
- Our discussion revealed that there are multiple different types of "groupwise" issues (I mostly describe the first one above. All might be useful but unfortunately probably vary substantially in implementation.)
  + Apply same checks _within_ groups
  + Apply different checks (or parameters for checks) dependent on groups
