title: Questions: Maximum value in a column and comparing keys across tables
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [ ] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.
* [ ] For any problems you identify, a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot. A reproducible example is:
    * [ ] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [ ] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [ ] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

## Question

This is a great package, and a promising R-based equivalent of Great Expectations in Python. However, when building ML pipelines there are a set of transforms and tests that come up frequently, but these do not _seem_ to be available in `pointblank` at this point in time:

* **Maximum value of a column** -- Generally, I want to determine if the maximum value of a date column is yesterday. This is a breaking condition to prevent models being trained if the latest transactions haven't been received. 

* **Consistency of keys between tables** -- When applying _transforms_ to data it is often desired to ensure that all of the keys in table A are present in table B; i.e, if I train a model I want to ensure that all of the entries in my input table A have predictions in output table B. 

Are either of these operations possible within `pointblank` with the `col_vals_*` functions, perhaps in a way that I've not considered?

title: Speed up the `tbl_scan()` function, provide estimates of processing duration, and show progress
description: The `tbl_scan()` function does a lot but it can be slow at generating all of the data for its reporting. It would be great to speed up the different components of it, provide estimates of time to finish, and also present progress bars for each of the reporting modules. It might even be possible to get an up-front estimate of the time duration before committing to a full run. cc @kmasiello

title: Make it possible to change the language of a table scan without re-running `scan_data()`
description:
Although the `scan_data()` function allows for the setting of a language, we unfortunately have to re-run the function if we want to change the language. This can be a bit slow so it's a drag to do. It would be better to store all of the calculated data in a `tbl_scan` object and have an additional function for report generation so that more options on reporting output, including language, can be available.

The `get_agent_report()` allows for a setting of `lang` that can override the `lang` of the input object. Thank you @kmasiello for the suggestion.

title: Add ability to save the `scan_data()` report
description:
Scanning a table object with `scan_data()` is helpful when looking at the dataset for the first time or when inspecting it for data issues. However, the object obtained can't be saved to disk like an agent or informant with `x_write_disk()`. This would be incredibly useful especially since this object might be created rather slowly with `scan_data()`.

Thanks @kmasiello for suggesting this!

title: Capture all requested steps / checks regardless of if they match columns in current data
description:
## Description

This is a follow-on issue to #232. As summarized by @rich-iannone :

(1) the evaluation of expressions in columns should occur during rule creation
(2) the re-evaluation of expressions in columns should happen again during interrogation
(3) handle cases where no column is available during interrogation (i.e., skips the step but preserves it, unlike now)
(4) the expansion of validation steps might need to be reconsidered (e.g., step 1 that targets 3 columns might be resolved as steps 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3 in the reporting)

The motivation for this issue is that `pointblank` does not register steps for which the validation check has no relevant columns. However, this means a pipeline can become "brittle" when it is subsequently used (or written to YAML and reused) for a dataset whose columns have changed. 

## Reproducible example

The following example illustrates the current way `pointblank` captures steps:

``` r
library(pointblank)
tmpdir <- tempdir()
tmp <- gsub("////", "", tempfile(tmpdir = "", fileext = ".yml"))

create_agent(read_fn = ~data.frame(x_1 = 1, x_2 = 2, y_1 = 3)) %>%
  col_vals_gt(starts_with("x"), 10, step_id = 1) %>%
  col_vals_lt(starts_with("z"),  2, step_id = 2) %>%
  yaml_write(filename = tmp, path = tmpdir)

cat(readLines(file.path(tmpdir, tmp)), sep = "\n")
```

    #> read_fn: ~data.frame(x_1 = 1, x_2 = 2, y_1 = 3)
    #> tbl_name: ~
    #> label: '[2021-02-09|06:03:29]'
    #> locale: en
    #> steps:
    #> - col_vals_gt:
    #>     columns: starts_with("x")
    #>     value: 10.0

<sup>Created on 2021-02-09 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>


## Expected result

Ideally, pointblank should also register a step for our `starts_with('z")` check even though no variables in the specific dataset currently used with the agent start with "z".

## Session info

This issue is non session-specific. It was created using package version 0.6.0.9000

End the reproducible example with a call to `sessionInfo()` in the same session (e.g. `reprex(si = TRUE)`) and include the output.

title: Include field in agent that states whether brief was autogenerated
description: When a validation step is added to the agent object, the expectation text (the brief, a name I’d love to change in the future) is by default added immediately for the step in the `lang` of the agent (default is English). It would be good to know whether the text has been autogenerated or not. One reason is that when creating agent YAML, it’s not necessary to add the `brief` text if it’s just default text (only if it’s custom text). The same goes for taking YAML and re-creating the expressions to obtain an agent object.

title: Introduce workflow for running multiple YAML files for agents and informants
description:
Right now, on-disk YAML files that represent agents and/or informants can be used for perform interrogations or incorporations, respectively. This is great but extra code is required on the user’s behalf to do this for a collection of YAML files. What’s needed is some function that processes all the files and accepts some functions for the pre and post stages. 

One idea is to enforce a directory and file-naming convention but also allow for manual specification of the YAML file locations. Having a `pointblank` subdirectory in a project makes sense, otherwise the top-level could also be used (if the project is entirely about doing pointblank tasks). Underneath, there should be a few different subdirectories for different purposes. This will require some experimentation to get right but having `yaml` and `output` dirs makes sense right now. 

There needs to be some way for utilizing the outputs (which might be in the form of RDS) files. I imagine producing a single HTML document that shows all of the reporting for all data sources would be good. As would a shiny module for integration into a Shiny app.

title: Add functions to check if column values missing from set
description:
## Question

I'd like to be able to check whether a column value is missing from a set, eg. a date in a column is missing from a range of dates. Not that my date column has an NA/NULL value, rather I'd like to know that "2020-06-30" doesn't appear at all in a specified column. So, how would I check for this in the pointblank workflow?

## Reproducible example

```
library(tibble)
library(pointblank)

df <- tibble(x = letters[1:5])

range_vals <- letters[1:6]

df %>%
  create_agent() %>%
  col_vals_in_set(columns = vars(x), set = range_vals) %>%
  col_vals_not_in_set(columns = vars(x), set = range_vals) %>%
  interrogate()

# f is missing from the set
setdiff(range_vals, df$x)

```
With these two checks I confirm that A-E are in the set of A-F and that there are no values in `x` outside of A-F; both 100% pass/fail. But what I'd really like to be able to identify, is that F does not appear in `x`. Thoughts?

title: Create a testthat test file from an agent
description:
Given a pointblank agent object or an agent YAML file it would be interesting to have a function to generate a testthat test file (putting it in `tests/testthat` if certain conditions are met). This would split the steps into separate `expect_*()` statements and subdivide into cases for warnings/errors (based on WARN and STOP thresholds). 

With the file written, regular tests can be performed manually or in GitHub Actions. There should be an option for making the resulting file read-only, and whether to overwrite existing test files.

title: Support arrow datasets in `create_informant()`
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **pointblank**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

Since Spark and DBI dataframes are supported, it would be nice to also support [Arrow datasets](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/r/articles/dataset.html).

Currently, getting the right metadata (row number) requires all the data to be in memory, which defeats the purpose of Arrow datasets (which is why it can't be done using the `read_fn` param). 

Here is what I found when I tried to manually rig the output of `create_informant()`:
- `dims()` can be called on an Arrow dataset object to retrieve the dimensions of the table 
- calling `head()` on an Arrow dataset returns an object from which data types can be extracted (e.g. `head(ds)$columns[[1]]$type`) - these will be Arrow types, not R types, but there is a direct mapping. 
- R data types for columns could also be retrieved by `collect()`-ing the output of the `head()` call.

Additionally, it might also be useful to display the partitioning schema in the informant report - perhaps as an automatically generated `info_section()`?

title: Add the `file_tbl()` function to obtain tables from local or remote files
description:
Like the `db_tbl()` function (which simplifies the creation of a `tbl_dbi` object), we need the analogue function `file_tbl()` to generate a table from a compatible data file. These files could be in any of the CSV, TSV, RDA, or RDS formats. The `file` argument should take a URL or a local file path. The delimited files will be handled by `readr::read_csv()` and options for that call can be included in `...`.

Because many files will likely need to be tested in GitHub repositories, the `from_github()` helper function should be added to resolve a data file URL from a simple file path in the repo and the GitHub repository address (in the format `username/repo[/subdir][@ref|#pull|@*release]`).

Once the data file is transformed to a data table, some metadata about the table's origin should be attached to the `tbl_df` so that it can be automatically consumed by `create_agent()` and `create_informant()` (unless overridden).

title: Is there any way to suppress "Pointblank Information" header at the top of informant output table?
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Question
Is there any way to suppress "Pointblank Information" header at the top of informant output table?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46800811/104188499-ad879380-545c-11eb-80e8-f165026430d2.png)

AS a background, I'm putting 5-10 different informant tables in one page, (This is my subjective opinion but) I feel "Pointblank Information" headers for every table are bit busy and redundant. It would be nice to suppress these headers and make table names stand out more in some cases.

p.s. Thank you for creating this amazing package! I love to use and explore pointblank's features.

title: Anomaly detection in table values
description: It would be great for time-series data (or univariate data) to detect anomalous data in a table. This needs to work well with both data frames and database tables.

title: Give the `snip_list()` function options for sorting
description:
Recently, quite a few options were added to the `snip_list()` function. This *was great*, and it really helps to make lists quite a lot more presentable by default (along with having all those new options).

One thing that was missed were methods for sorting list items. Currently, the list is sorted by first appearance. There should be better options like sorting by frequency, or sequentially (alphabetically/numerically). And, there should also be a way to reverse the sort order.

title: Add a `snip_*()` function that creates inline stats summaries for a column
description:
While some of the `snip_*()` functions are OK for extracting portions of values from a column, it would be nice to get an inline five-number summary from a numerical column. We already make this possible `scan_data()` (and the code works across all DB types too), so we could use the same code path here. 

As well, the summary should be presented in a nice manner, with several styles (from pretty basic to rather fancy). On top of that, there should be an option to use an ‘alternate’ five number summary. Here are the two types:

1. MIN, Q1, MED, Q3, MAX
2. MEAN, SUM, SUM SQ., SAMPLE SD, POP SD

As yet another option, we could add on the N and number of missing values.

title: Give the `snip_list()` function more options
description:
Right now, the `snip_list()` function (usable within `info_snippet()`) has a dearth of options for generating a list (with only `limit` available). This should be expanded so that lists generated from column data in information reports:

1. have a better default appearance
2. can be easily customized
3. can be localized to different languages

As a starting point, the following options might be included:

- `sep`: the separator to use between items (default:  `","`)
- `and_or`: the conjunction to use in a list with items > 2; could be `NULL` (sets to `"and"`), `"and"`, `"or"`, or `""` (default: `NULL`)
- `oxford`: whether a list with items >2 should use the mandatory serial comma, only when the language is English (default: `TRUE`)
- `as_code`: whether to set the items in a code font (default: `TRUE`)
- `quot_str`: whether to use quotation marks around each list item; could be `TRUE`/`FALSE` but `NULL` decides based on the vector type (default: `NULL`)

title: Minor error in cojointly() examples documentation
description:
From: [https://rich-iannone.github.io/pointblank/reference/conjointly.html#examples](url)

The comments in the example state that the first validation test in the group is:

(1) values in `a` are less than `4`

While the rest of the example code shows:

```
    ~ col_vals_lt(., vars(a), 8),
```

Presumably, example text should read:

(1) values in `a` are less than `8`

Incredibly minor, but enough to throw me off for a couple of minutes.

title: Translate validation checks into human-readable descriptions
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **pointblank**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

`pointblank` creates amazing, aesthetic documentation. However, it might also be useful to be able to automate documentation in human-readable plain text (e.g. details in a data dictionary). To enable this, it could be useful to have some sort of `translate()` function that can parse validation checks. For example:

```
translate(col_vals_between(agent, starts_with("N"), left = 0, right = 9, inclusive = c(TRUE, FALSE)))
```

might return something like 

> Column between 0 (inclusive) and 9 (exclusive)

I can imagine multiple ways that this function could work. For example, such a function might either take the validation functions directly (as shown above) or it could take the `agent` object and return a dataframe with one row per check and one column with the "code" version and one with the plaintext.

title: Preserve select helpers when translating to YAML
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **pointblank**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

Currently, YAML translation functions evaluate the select helpers and record the specific realizations in the dataset. For example, in the following reprex, I configure the check with `starts_with("date")` but the resulting YAML file instead shows the check specifically for the variables `date` and `datetime` which match the helper. 

``` r
library(pointblank)

agent <- 
  create_agent(read_fn = ~small_table) %>%
  col_is_date(starts_with("date"))

yaml_agent_string(agent)
```

    #> read_fn: ~small_table
    #> tbl_name: .na.character
    #> label: '[2020-11-18|17:45:00]'
    #> locale: en
    #> steps:
    #> - col_is_date:
    #>     columns: vars(date_time)
    #> - col_is_date:
    #>     columns: vars(date)

<sup>Created on 2020-11-18 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

To support a "roundtrip" or to support greater portability of config files (e.g. use the same YAML file to validate multiple tables; or continue to use a YAML file as columns are added to a table), it would be more helpful to preserve the select helpers in the YAML, e.g

    #> steps:
    #> - col_is_date:
    #>     columns: starts_with("date")


This is related to #218 in that it supports a round-trip. However, I'm opening a new issue since this is a specific feature besides the tests, and @rich-iannone suggested I open an issue on discussion.

title: Have different grouping options for the agent report
description:
The agent report currently has a few rudimentary options for filtering/arranging validation steps by failure condition. However it would be great to take this a step further and include options for grouping validation steps. The grouping can be made across validation types (row-based, column-based, whole table, etc.), and also by the columns themselves (groups for each column).

For validation plans with lots of steps, this last method of grouping will make the reporting much easier to parse and to locate the results of interest.

title: Display a tally of highest failure condition reached across all steps in the agent report
description: Especially for larger validation agent reports it would be useful to have a very minimal tally of total steps, and the number of steps reaching each of the W, S, and N conditions. Also, it would be great to show how many actions are fired (both stepwise and at the end). This last part will require some upfront work to record successful/failed evaluations of any set action functions.

title: Display the processing time of each validation step in the agent report
description: It would be useful to (somewhere) show the amount of time taken to process each step of the validation plan in the agent report. This might be inside of a CSS tooltip attached to the color strips on the left of the table but perhaps there are other options.

title: Include a visualization for column schema matching
description:
Right now, if a `col_schema_match()` validation step fails, there’s no insight into where the failure occurred (there’s simply 1 failed test unit and that’s it). It would be much better if we can see where the mismatches occurred.

There could be a custom function that gets this in a tabular format, along with a knitr print method. Also, this should be shown in the agent report.

title: Allow use of a custom SQL expression as value for any `preconditions` argument
description: Using `preconditions` in a validation step allows for the temporary (just for the current step) mutation of the target table. Right now any R code can be put in an R formula (RHS). It would be great, for databases or Spark tables, to have the option to use SQL for the temp table transformation. Like in #224 , we would use the reexported `dbplyr::sql()` function to signify that SQL is to be used. An internal error (captured, displayed in agent report) would result if SQL was used for a data frame or if there was a query error.

title: Allow use of a custom SQL expression in `col_vals_expr()`
description:
Right now the `col_vals_expr()` allows for an expression (either in the form of a call made with the `expr()` function or as a one-sided R formula using a leading `~`) but it would be useful for the input to be an SQL expression (so long as the target table is a database or Spark table).

We can reexport the `dbplyr::sql()` function for this, requiring its use in the `expr` argument. The `dbplyr::is_sql()` can be used to check whether the input is SQL. During the interrogation phase, it'll then be possible to verify that the data source is a database or Spark table. We can have internal error (captured for the validation step) if this isn't the case.

title: Add a console print method for `action_levels()`
description: When printing the output list of `action_levels()`, the list easily fills a screen and it’s hard to parse quickly. It would be much better if this object printed nicely in the console, and surfaced information about which thresholds are set, the threshold values, the type of failure threshold (relative or absolute), and the connected actions.

title: Allow use of select helpers in `col_exists()`
description: Allowing `col_exists()` to use select helpers would be useful for checking the presence of columns that match a pattern or begin with a known prefix.

title: Have an option to skip a validation step if the target column is missing
description:
It can happen that a column isn't available for a validation check in some circumstances. Further to this, it might be difficult to check for the existence of the column (and it might have to be done outside of the pointblank API). The validation step should still be present but having the interrogation risk failure and possibly trigger some undesired notification is not ideal.

There is an `active` argument which skips a validation step if the value is `FALSE`. If we make available a helper function that automatically skips a step based on the presence of the target column, the aforementioned situation can be better managed. The helper function might be named `if_col_present()`, and it should be allowed for use in `active` arg of each validation function that operates on a target column.

title: Ensure that agent objects are identical when making a round trip to YAML and back
description: A pointblank agent can be written to YAML (even alongside a pointblank informant) and furthermore an agent can be generated from YAML (the agent-specific portion). What needs to be extensively tested is the fidelity of the agent object when written to YAML and then created again from that YAML. We need to ensure that no information is lost and none gets mutated or inadvertantly added during this round trip.

title: get_sundered_data fails when type = "combined" AND using preconditions
description:
## Description

`get_sundered_data` fails with `Error in eval(lhs, parent, parent) : object tbl_check_join not found` when run with `type = "combined"` and preconditions are specified in a test.

Problem does not happen if either:

* preconditions are not set
* `fail` or `pass` is specified for `type` NOTE that specifying `fail` returns erroneous results - it fails to return the failed rows  

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(pointblank)

result <- 
  small_table %>% 
  create_agent() %>% 
  col_vals_equal(e, "TRUE",
                 preconditions = ~ . %>% 
                   dplyr::filter(f == "high"),
                 brief = "e is TRUE") %>% 
  interrogate()
 
get_sundered_data(result, type = "combined")
```

    #> Error in eval(lhs, parent, parent): object 'tbl_check_join' not found

<sup>Created on 2020-10-14 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>


## Expected result

a tibble should have been printed that matches original data, with a new column, `.pb_combined` containing `pass` and `fail`
values.

title: Compile an information report to roxygen-compatible text for dataset documentation
description: The informant could get an output mode that provides text for roxygen documentation. This would be ideal for documentation of datasets in a package.

title: Add column SQL types in addition to R column types in information report
description: When generating table information for database tables, column types shown are just the R column types. However, it would be much more useful to have both the SQL types and then the R types (e.g., `VARCHAR -> character`). Later on, when the package collects info on whether DB table columns are nullable, that should be displayed as well.

title: Document `Text Tricks` in docs for each `info_*()` function
description: There is a collection of text tricks that can be used when creating info text. A paragraph briefly explaining how to use these should be included in each of the `info_*()` functions that deal expressly with adding info text.

title: Supply a shiny app to help generate a validation plan
description:
A shiny app for **pointblank** validations should be developed and the initial release should only have the ability to generate a validation plan. The useful output would be R statements that can be placed into a new .R file and a YAML file with the validation plan (interrogations can executed directly from YAML).

Useful features are: 

- a small preview of the dataset
- help in defining a `read_fn` (with a preview of the read-in table)
- optimized interfaces for each validation type
- a preview of the in-progress validation plan
- help with defining threshold levels and per-step actions
- help with defining end functions (`end_fns`)
- profiling of the dataset and adding validation step stubs

There is definitely a lot more that could be done but even these features would require a lot of work.

title: Create a "Security Requirements" article
description: Create an article that describes what the user can and cannot expect in terms of security (a "Security Requirements" document). This should go into detail about database credentials, how they are to be used with the package, and that they are not stored in any artifacts created by **pointblank**.

title: Create article on software architecture
description: There needs to be an article explaining the high-level design (i.e., software architecture) of the **pointblank** package. This should be segmented by the major workflows (e.g., validation, information, testing, expectations, etc.). Explanations should be easy to read, with enough detail to understand how the internals work.

title: Create a project roadmap and display it in the project README
description:
A project roadmap should be created and displayed in the README. This needs to be a visual roadmap that can be changed frequently without too much difficulty. There should be enough information in the graphic to determine what will be worked on for the next three releases. Furthermore, each work package should display its status:

- `proposed`
- `approved`
- `in progress`
- `delivered`

Releases should have estimates for timing and any `in progress` items should display the amount of work completed.

title: Fulfill criteria for attaining Silver Status in the OpenSSF Best Practices Badge Program
description: The project is close to attaining all requirements for Silver Status in the CII Best Practices Badge Program (https://bestpractices.coreinfrastructure.org/en). Only a few tasks remain to get to this level but they will be tracked under separate issues since the amount of work for each is pretty substantial.

title: Function to read a collection of saved validations and make a report
description:
Thank you for making this package. It really is incredible!

 I have a request that I hope you consider a good idea. I have a workflow where the validation is performed daily and saved to a directory. We are very interested in tracking validation metrics over time. So, the validation report would be one that has a bar graph for each validation step. At least for our purposes, this would be incredibly valuable. Thank you Rich.

title: Unclear how to specify a negative condition conjointly
description:
I am perhaps missing something, but it's difficult to express a negative joint condition across rows. For example, I want to verify that if var1 is "J", var2 should be **neither** "F" or "N". So I need the last two rows and only the last two rows to fail here:

``` r
library(pointblank)

tbl <- dplyr::tibble(
  var1 = c("J", "J", "J", "A", "J", "J"),
  var2 = c("R", "R", "R", "B", "F", "N")
)

tbl %>% 
  conjointly(
    ~ col_vals_equal(., vars(var1), "J"),
    ~ col_vals_not_in_set(., vars(var2), c("F","N"))
  ) 
```

    #> Error: Exceedance of failed test units where there should have been conjoint 'pass' units across the following expressions: `~col_vals_equal(., vars(var1), "J")`, `~col_vals_not_in_set(., vars(var2), c("F", "N"))`.
    #> The `conjointly()` validation failed beyond the absolute threshold level (1).
    #> * failure level (3) >= failure threshold (1)

<sup>Created on 2020-09-21 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0.9001)</sup>

Would a batch of `*_not_conjointly` functions be unnecessary? I feel like I'm missing something simple.

title: A few non-translated tooltips remain in the agent report
description: There are tooltips in the EVAL and TBL columns of the agent report that are still untranslated.

title: Have the option to email the informant report
description:
Right now, the agent report (a **gt** table that reports on a validation) can be put into a **blastula** email object and emailed (as part of an interrogation or in post). It would be great if an informant report (another **gt** table, this time with information about a data table) could also be emailed. 

We could make the informant object compatible with the existing emailing functions. Also, it would be good to have a smaller size (decreased width) version of the informant report.

title: Capture warnings/errors from `info_snippet()` fns
description:
When building up table information through an informant, you can specify functions to invoke at `incorporate()` time. This is great because you can glean info from a changing-over-time table and put those results into the info text. However, what if one or more of those functions fails?

We don’t want to stop the process entirely but we do want to report on these evaluation problems so that they can be fixed by the user. Fortunately, this is a solved problem in the data validation workflow. We use an internal function to evaluate certain functions and capture any error/warnings. So, this methodology needs to be brought over to the information management workflow.

title: Add unseen columns to informant upon `incorporate()`
description:
As tables may change between uses of `incorporate()`, the *informant* currently only updates dimension values (column and row counts) but doesn’t update the `columns` section with the names of new columns. This should be done, perhaps updating the order of columns as well.

On top of this, some columns from a target table might be dropped or renamed over time. We need some ways to handle these changes without losing information. That’ll be a different issue though.

title: Add Russian translation
Checking relational data without joining manually before / reflect data structure in data dictionary
description:
This is the follow-up from https://twitter.com/riannone/status/1305399926617145344.

---

I have data which is structured like a relational database using several distinct tables. Thus, many values need to be checked across two or more tables of the data structure.

One solution would be to join the tables in question before creating an agent. However, it would be nice if it was possible to somehow reference the other tables needed without joining explicitly. 

I think this would also help in describing the checks in a YAML file / data dictionary. But this would need to be a slightly different kind of YAML than the one described in #149. One solution might be to include a `columns` section for each table of the full relational structure in the YAML, like:

```yaml
tab1:
  columns:
    id:
      label: A short label.
      type: character
      info: An ID column. Can be used to merge tab1 with tab2.
    column_1:
      label: A short label.
      type: numeric
      info: Extended information about the column.
    ...

tab2:
  columns:
    id:
      label: A short label.
      type: character
      info: An ID column. Can be used to merge tab2 with tab1.
    column_2:
      label: A short label.
      type: numeric
      info: Extended information about the column.
    ...
```

Then, one could reference variables from other table with tab$var or tab[[var]] for example. But one would have to describe the relations of the different tables as well, otherwise joining the tables automatically in the backgroud would not work. Here's a rough example of what I mean:

```yaml
relations:
  tab_1: tab1
  tab_2: tab2
  type: 1:n
  key_1: id
  key_2: id
```

This sounds like a lot of work but would greatly enhance the purpose of the YAML serving as a data dictionary.

title: Add an `incorporate()` function for informant objects
description:
Table information is useful even at this early stage but would be even better if it were to access the target table and update information about the table. To do that, we need an `incorporate()` function.

To do this effectively, we need to a way to express the set of queries and integrate that with the metadata strings. This would work in a similar manner to interrogations in the data validation flow. Things we need:

1. ~~Way to express functions. Probably a named list with the names serving as query IDs and the RHS holding the expressions~~
2. ~~A way to insert the query results into the text. The `{query_id}` approach might work well here.~~ 
3. Storage for the rendered string and timestamps for modification date-time
4. Storage for logs of `incorporate()`s

title: Add function to *remove* one or more validation steps
description:
If repurposing an agent for an updated table (or a similar but different table) it might be useful to read in an agent with a validation plan but strategically remove steps that don’t work in the new context.

We can already modify the agent’s `read_fn` and set a table with `set_tbl()` for interactive validations with an agent, so modifying the validation plan is an extension of this.

An open question is how to target the steps for removal. This could be done with step indices, with steps that target/involve certain columns (so select helpers could be used), and maybe some other ways.

title: Add function to create a table metadata object
description:
The `create_metadata()` function will create a `ptblank_metadata` object that is similar to `create_agent()`. Then add functions for facilitating entry of metadata elements (for individual columns, the table, misc. fields, etc.).

Printing the metadata object should show the metadata report. We should be able to write the object to YAML using `yaml_write()`.

title: Translate text in agent report that refers to the extract CSV
description: The text is hardcoded in English only but should be translated to all supported languages. The numeric value should also be formatted according the the chosen locale.

title: chinese translation
description: same as #174

title: portuguese translation
description: I'll leave the idea here and I'll be editing files.

title: For column metadata (w/ databases, Spark) include the `nullable` property
description:
We can define a schema in `col_schema()` for use in `col_schema_match()` but there is no way to check the nullable state of columns in databases or in Spark schemas. This should be added in.

On top of this, `nullable` needs to be a recognized field for columns in metadata YAML. The `meta_yaml_write()` function should generate a TRUE/FALSE for `_nullable` when appropriate, and, it needs to be recognized by the `get_metadata_report()` function and put into the report in a sensible way.

title: Incorporate a `locale` option to determine formatting of numbers in reporting outputs
description:
The table scan (from `scan_data()`), the agent report (from `get_agent_report()`, or printing the *agent*), and the table metadata report (from `get_metadata_report()`) all have the potential to present large numbers (e.g., row counts) and numbers with decimals (e.g., relative failure thresholds) but there is presently no use of digit separators, and, the decimal separator is always a `.`.

With a `locale` option, we can better format numbers in all of these report products. Where to add? Some good functions for this: `create_agent()`, `scan_data()`, and `meta_yaml_write()`.

title: Non-destructively enhance/update metadata YAML with table properties
description:
Say you have a metadata YAML file for a table and you like it very much. Wouldn't it be nice if a function were to augment (enhance?) the YAML with table properties without messing up what you already have? The design of metadata YAML already has in it the idea that **pointblank**-generated fields begin with an underscore (preferring that metadata value if the non-underscore property also exists), so this could be isolated to add/update those `_*` fields.

Other ideas:
  - add missing columns to the `columns` section (or add the section if not present)
  - add modification timestamps (this is not a thing yet, but could be manageable for just those `_*` fields
  - optionally add a log entry to the `changes` section (create section if not present, of course) with each update + plus short description of changes
  - optionally reorder column entries if column ordering has changed

title: Have `conjointly()` also work with `col_is_*()` validation functions
description: Right now, any validation functions used in `conjointly()` must be of the `col_vals_*()` set. However, it would be great to have any of the `col_is_*()` function allowed as well.

title: Improve documentation for pointblank YAML
description:
YAML can now be produced from a pointblank agent or informant. However the documentation around this feature is very minimal.

There needs to be function documentation for the two exported functions. Also, a vignette/article would be useful here.

title: Develop benchmarks for agent validations
description: This will involve taking a standard table (with different storage types) and running against a standard set of validations. The results can be put into a table, possibly part of a vignette/article.

title: The `end_fns` argument of `create_agent()` is poorly explained
description: The `end_fns` argument of `create_agent()` requires quite a lot more explanation and some examples. This argument is critical for sending an email of the agent report based on values obtained from the interrogation. Aside from that specific case, any side effect can be used (or not) based on the data gained from an interrogation. The documentation currently doesn’t make that apparent at all.

title: Add an execution completion timestamp to the agent
description: To determine the total duration of time for the interrogation, we need to record the execution completion timestamp in the agent object. This will allow for a measure of time elapsed even for an interrogation with no validation steps (each step currently records a start time and a duration when complete) since there may be some overhead even before interrogation of the first validation step.

title: Reporting of interval values for `col_vals_between()`/`col_vals_not_between()` should use ISO 31-11 notation
description:
In the agent report, the values for validation steps created with `col_vals_between()` and `col_vals_not_between()` are simply comma-separated values (in the `VALUES` column). However, these functions allow for specification of closed, open, and half-open intervals (on either side). We should instead denote these values with parentheses and square brackets (using ISO 31-11). Examples are

```
[1, 8]
(1, 8]
[1, 8)
(1, 8)
```

which give the closed interval (`inclusive` as `c(TRUE, TRUE)`, the default), left half-open interval (right bound is inclusive), right half-open interval (left bound is inclusive), and open interval (`inclusive` as `c(FALSE, FALSE)`).

title: Data dictionary (involving pointblank YAML)
description:
From issue #134 @Plebejer provides good ideas on ways to describe table columns in YAML. The new pointblank YAML feature could serve as a data dictionary (way to describe columns, the dataset itself, meaning of rows, etc.). 

The structure of defining columns in pointblank YAML might be:

```
columns:
  column_1:
    label: A short label.
    type: numeric
    info: Extended information about the column.
  ...
```

There also needs to be functions that could be used to generate this YAML file, a YAML snippet, and a way to extract the `columns` data into some text that can be used as R documentation on datasets.

Generating the YAML can be done with a table, an agent (in memory or on disk), an x-list, etc. Making a YAML template also seems like a good idea. Once generated, there should be a way to update/enrich the metadata (through scanning of the source data). The fields that pointblank generates should complement the user-defined fields (and not be destructive). 

The YAML file can/should be used to generate a reporting table for the table metadata. It ought to look and feel similar to the pointblank agent report.

title: Add a `label` field for each of the validation steps
description:
Having a `label` field would be a nice addition for validation steps in an agent-based workflow. Right now, in the agent reporting, the steps are denoted by the names of the validation functions used to generate the validation steps. This can make the report difficult to read and perhaps less useful if we already have our own identifiers.

The `label` should have no bearing on the agent-less workflow, and it won't be an argument in the `expect_*()` or `test_*()` analogues of the validation functions. Should a label be provided, it will replace the name of the validation function in the `STEP` column in the agent report.

title: create agents from file, list or data.frame
description:
Hi Rich,

this is the follow-up Issue to our Twitter conversation: https://twitter.com/riannone/status/1281491772028452864. I would like to divide the possibilities I've though of into two separate approaches.

# rule-focused approach
First, in case you haven't seen it yet, [this](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/validate/vignettes/rule_files.html) is the vignette which describes how importing and exporting of validation rules works in [validate](https://github.com/data-cleaning/validate). I have used this and I think it works pretty well. I think it is especially helpful that you can import validation rules from a variety of sources, like `yaml`, but also `data.frame`s.

I would describe this a a rule-focused approach, since each item in the `yaml` represents a single validation rule.


# variable-focused approach
What I'm working on right now is more a variable-focused approach. What I mean by that is that we describe our data using a `metadata.yaml` file. This file contains some general information about the dataset in question and a section on `columns`: This section looks like this:

```yaml
columns:
  VAR1:
    label: Short label
    notes: Some longer notes
    constraints:
    - type: integer
    - greater-than: 0
    - not-null: yes
    ....

  VAR2:
    ...
```

Here, each item in `constraints` needs to correspond to a pointblank validation function. (Since pointblank does not yet cover all of our needs, we bridge the gap with custom functions which translate our needs to `col_vals_expr()`) 

This is also, where my question on Twitter was coming from: When I read that `yaml` into a list, it is easy to create an agent for each `constraints` element of each column. But reducing them is not yet possible. (I fall back to a R-unlike approach, where I loop through all list elements and add the resulting validation functions step by step to an agent which was created before.)

The advantage of this variable-focused approach (imho) is, that it is easier for people to see which constraints apply to a specific variable and if anything is missing. Also, this might make it possible for the `yaml` file to carry additional information about the column which might be of interest at some other point in the pipeline (this is the case in our scenario).

On the other hand, in this approach it is not straight-forward how to describe rules which apply to the whole dataset, like `nrow(data) > 1000`. Also, it may result in more typing since functions like `cols_not_null()` are likely to apply to several columns, which would easier/shorter to describe in a rule-focused approach (see the section on "Groups" in `?validate::syntax`).


# general thoughts

As I've mentioned above, it would be very helpful if reading validation rules would be possible from different sources, like `yaml`, but also from R objects like `data.frame`s or `list`s. This would make it possible to "translate" other formats of storing the validation functions into a format which can be understood by pointblank within R.

Please ask for clarification, if this is unclear at some point!

title: Identify the type of table being validated in the agent report (tibble, database)

Hey Rich, this is a **very** useful package. Data quality is a big concern for our group and so this package is now central to our analytics processes. I really cannot thank you enough for the excellent work you put into this package!

title: "Composite" validation functions ?
description:
Hi @rich-iannone 

I've got a conceptual question about whether and how to "compose" validation functions in order to simplify an industry-specific data quality or data pipeline analysis.

Let's use a consumer finance industry example - making loans to borrowers.  Assume I have a bunch of "loan"-related tables in my remote database that track variables such as original_loan_amount, the current_loan_amount, the original_interest_rate, the current_interest_rate, the original_payment, the current_payment, and a number of other related variables.  I'd like to take the "core" validation functions from `pointblank`, such as `col_vals_between` and `col_vals_not_null`, and create "composite" validation functions specific to my finance industry use case.  

For example, given the "loan"-related tables described above, there will be a large number of variables across my tables that contain variations of "payment" (i.e.,  "original_payment", "current_payment", etc).  Therefore, I'd like to build a "composite" validation function called `col_vals_payment` that I can apply to all "payment"-related columns in the data, which would include a number of "core" validation functions tailored to my finance industry use case:

- `col_vals_between` $0 and $1,000; (our loans never have payments over $1000/mo)
- `col_vals_lte` the value of the "current_balance"; (you can't pay more than you owe)
-  `col_vals_equals` 0 when "current_balance" equals 0; (no need to make payments once loan is paid off)
- etc, etc

From your viewpoint as the package designer, does it make sense to construct these kind of "composite" validation functions?  If so, do you have a recommended method for building such functions?

Thanks for the advice!
Kyle

title: Create a `step_id` for each validation step
description:
As a preparatory step for moving toward a continuous data validation feature, we need to have a `step_id` argument for each validation step. This will allow us to develop data lineage across multiple runs on a data source. Even as more steps are added for a data source over time, existing steps can still be identified and monitored over consecutive runs.

The `step_id` argument will have a default value of `NULL`. If nothing is provided, then the value will be based on the step index (e.g., `0001`). In this way, even as new steps are added (at the end of the index), existing steps should still be traceable over time.

title: col_schema: less strict matching of types and no type matching
description:
I really love the col_schema_match() function and its helper function col_schema(). It's helping to ensure that the columns and types for a transformed table are exactly what we think they should be.

There are some possible enhancements for col_schema(), all in the name of making this less strict (good in some circumstances):

1. Have an option to use all_of() and any_of() for the column types. Columns like datetime have POSIXct and POSIXt and it would be nice to just specify one of those with any_of("POSIXct")

2. Have it so we don't need to specify the column types (if we just want to ensure the column names are present)

Thanks again for your awesome work in this really awesome package! Like I said before, it is such an incredible contribution.

title: Writing validation results to a file
description:
I'd like to have the validation results stored as a file. This way we can recall a past data quality validation run and compare with a recent run. Is this something that you're already thinking about doing? 

Thanks!

description: Right now, `tbl_dbi` table objects are disallowed from use in `scan_data()`. Reason for this is that I couldn’t verify that the dplyr statements would generate valid SQL for the summary stats. The next phase with `scan_data()` is to make it work with any `tbl_dbi` object, aiming for high compatibility with different DB types.

title: Verification of translations and improvements
description:
Translations exist for the agent report and for the output generated from the `scan_data()` function (e.g., https://rpubs.com/rich_i/pointblank_storms_german). However, the translations are not yet verified for accuracy. Also, there is no method to allow us to see all of the translated text in the agent report or in the `scan_data()` report.

A thing to do here is to generate a function that will visualize all of the strings so that they are be verified and improved upon. This will make things easier in the future, as well, when we might want to add more of them or translate to new languages. The function will essentially generate a gt table or two with the translated text in the reporting language of choice.

Languages that need verification are:

- [ ] French
- [x] German
- [ ] Italian
- [x] Spanish

Tooltips in the agent report are currently not translated. Neither are console messages during interrogation in an interactive session.

Another future improvement has to do with the storage and retrieval of the translation strings. It would be better if they were available in files so that Unicode code points don't need to be used (conversion would happen after reading).

title: New CRAN release?
description:
This package is wonderful, I can't say that enough. However I'm wondering if there is a new CRAN release in the works? There are some excellent features that are currently only in the GitHub version and it would be good to have them available for all in an official CRAN release.

Thank you for working on this really awesome package!!! Super happy with all it's been able to help me with .

title: Add the `col_vals_like()` function
description:
The `col_vals_like()` function will work much like the `col_vals_regex()` function except it will use globbed matching expressions. This is most useful in database tables (where the `LIKE` operator is commonly used) but it should still be useful for data frames. Note that this operator is not universal across some DB types. 

In the second case, the globbed expression should be converted to a regular expression with `glob2rx()` and interrogation will be done through the regex matching codepath.

title: `col_vals_regex()` not permitted for DB tables, but should be supported
description: While regex support differs across DBs, it is widely supported. It should be permitted and shouldn’t result in stopping the validation. The implementation for each DB will indeed vary but any error should be caught during the interrogation and placed in the capture stack.

title: The `col_schema()` function doesn't lowercase SQL column types, potentially resulting in failed validations of SQL column types
description: The `col_schema()` function allows you to specifying SQL column types (using `.db_col_types = "sql"`) but it's common to write these types as uppercase (e.g., "INT", "TINYINT", etc.). This will always fail validation because we (rightfully) lowercase the SQL types during the `create_agent()` call. To fix, we should lowercase the user-submitted types in `col_schema()` (but only when the `.db_col_types = "sql"` option is present). I don't believe at present that any SQL column types have mixed types (like the `"Date"` class in R).

title: Tooltips for all parts of the report table
description:
I really think this package is awesome and I'm using it constantly. It's the only R package that makes data checking both easy and really rigorous. I have to check a lot of datasets and find out what problems they have and this package seriously has all the tools for the job. Thanks for all the great work you're putting into it!!!

A feature request I'd like to make here is to have tooltips put on all of the different cells of the report table. If there there are a lot of values in a cell, the report only shows the first part of it and then ... . But a tooltip could provide a bit more info (could still be a high level summary).

Thank you  again. This is one of the best R packages around and it's still always getting better!

title: Add the `col_vals_expr()` function
description:
The `col_vals_expr()` function should be implemented for DIY validations (along with the expectation and test function forms). This will be great in situations where the specific `col_vals_*()` are too simplistic. 

We should be able to supply R expressions as formulas or in `expr()` (which will be re-exported). Expressions supplied should evaluate to logical and an interesting use case for all this would be `case_when()` expressions (this is another function that will be re-exported).

title: Add the `col_vals_increasing()` and `col_vals_decreasing()` functions
description:
These functions would validate for whether values are increasing or decreasing. Any NA/NULL values can be excluded with`na_pass`. 

Whether to accept stationary values as passing should be an option. Further to this, a tolerance distance (for movement in the opposite direction) should be available.

title: Better printing of values for `col_vals_between()` and `col_vals_not_between()` in agent reports
description: Right now, only single, literal values are allowed. This is in contrast to the other, single comparison validation functions that allow the use of a literal value and a column of values. There should be four allowable possibilities in total that comprise the different combinations of column/literal values per side.

title: Example not working (?)
description:
Hi! I a friend recommended me the package and I wanted to try it out. However, after trying this example

![Example](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25235690/82119709-5c48c800-9746-11ea-9870-89318d2c078a.png)

I had some issues rendering the .html document, with this result:

Any idea why it might be happening? I also had some troubles running the next example because of the function 'stop_if_not'.

Thanks!

title: Snapshot Validation
description:
This is a feature request.

A common pattern I use for validating complex data pipelines is snapshotting a working implementation into an output directory to use as reference. Any major refactors would result in spitting out a new snapshot, and diffing against the reference one.

This is helpful because I painstakingly verify the data pipeline upon first implementation, but don't have the bandwidth to do so for each refactor.

I can imagine a workflow where agents could redirect to an output directory at key points in a data pipeline to be used as reference data in the future.

title: download option for rows that do not pass validations?
description:
I'm in the process of validating several large datasets. I demo'd pointblank to great interest, but someone asked if I could include the option to download a csv of the rows that fail certain conditions. I then tried to rig up some chunks like:

```
{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(pointblank)
library(downloadthis)
```

``` 
{r validate = TRUE}
test1 <- try(col_vals_gt(iris, vars(Sepal.Length), 6), silent = TRUE)
if (inherits(test1, "try-error")) {
  download_this(
    subset(iris, Sepal.Length < 6),
    output_name = "test1 failed rows",
    output_extension = ".csv",
    button_label = "Download data",
    button_type = "warning",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa fa-save"
  )
}

```
But this fails with error:
`Error in if (!error_vec[i]) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed``

The chunks run if I remove the `validate = TRUE` chunk option, but I want to preserve that magic. Is there a way I can get the best of both worlds? Perform validations and include download options?

title: `scan_data` function documentation
description:
Hi @rich-iannone,

Loving the new developments in the `pointblank` package.  Just FYI, the `scan_data` [function documentation](https://rich-iannone.github.io/pointblank/reference/scan_data.html) currently states that the "tbl" argument "can be a data frame, a tibble, or a tbl_dbi object".  However, the [function code](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/aa30c3252cf7431b561a48ca6c5f1109a887f76c/R/scan_data.R#L57) specifically precludes tbl_dbi's as inputs.

The function is truly awesome, so I'm hoping that applying it to tbl_dbi's is a work-in-progress.  :) Regardless, I just wanted to give you the heads up.  Thanks for all the hard work.

Best
Kyle

title: Add RMarkdown template files
description: Add RMarkdown template files and a function to create a file. These are to be used with a data quality workflow. Add code chunks suited for: (1) setup, (2) validation code, (3) reporting, and (4) emailing options (Connect or through SMTP).

title: suggestion for col_schema improvements
description:
Rich, first of all this is an incredible package.... we are heavily invested in using it in production. We are now, on a daily basis, checking the data quality of about 80 DB tables and this package (a complete system really) provides everything we need to ensure we are on top of issues. We definitely wouldn't have caught so many problems without this package, it's now indispensable. Anyway enough gushing just know that we are appreciative.

This brings me to my feature request idea.. with the newest cran release of pointblank there is now the ability to validate table schemas. We definitely needed this and there are plans to revise our pointblank scripts to include this. One possibility to make this better is to include some more options in col_schema (the function that is used to define the schema). One option could be to either enforce a strict ordering of columns as defined, or, make the order not essential (like %in%). One more option would be to have the columns specified not necessarily the entire set of columns in the table (an 'at least' idea). I know that would make the schema definition less strict but this is useful in some cases and could be exposed as useful options.

title: Release pointblank 0.3.1
description:
- [x] If not a new package, make sure any warnings/errors in CRAN check results page are fixed

- [x] Create a GitHub issue called "Release checklist for [version]". Include the steps below as checklist steps.

- [x] Create branch labelled v[version]-rc, for example, v1.5.2-rc (the "rc" stands for "Release Candidate").

- [x] Change the DESCRIPTION and NEWS on this branch to change the version number to the desired version for CRAN, e.g. from 1.5.1.9008 to 1.5.2.

- [x] Commit and push to the RC branch.

- [x] Clean your package directory to remove any extraneous files, including ones that are git-ignored. (Warning, this will delete any unsaved buffers in RStudio! Also, be sure to close RStudio before taking this step!) git clean -xdf .

- [x] Build your package. I (jcheng) personally do it from the Mac command line like this:
PATH=$PATH:/Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/pandoc R CMD build [pkgdir]

- [x] Do a sanity check by installing/testing the built package.

- [x] Perform revdep check using https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck, if this is not the initial CRAN release.

- [x] Run R CMD check --as-cran pkg_version.tar.gz both locally and on win-builder.

- [x] Read every bullet point in the CRAN Policies document if this is the first release of the package. I usually print it out and check off the items one by one.

- [x] Submit to CRAN via their online form.

- [x] If there are R CMD check warnings that are unavoidable, make sure to explain them in the comments.

- [x] If rejected, make changes on the RC branch and bump the fourth (patch) version component, i.e. 1.5.2.1.

- [x] When accepted, tag the RC branch with a v1.5.2.1 tag (or whatever version you finally ended up getting accepted), and push the tag to origin.

- [x] Merge RC into master.

- [x] On master, change the package version to 1.5.2.9000.

title: A question about the `scan_data()` function
description:
I tried out the new function `scan_data()` on some of my data tables at work. It's really great as it is and actually has so much more potential. Just wondering if the HTML can be included in a Connect-based Rmarkdown report?

It would be killer to share daily summaries of changing datasets with Connect in this way. By the way, we are using the validation stuff in this package to great effect. Everyone's pretty impressed with the results from this package and I'm teaching people how to use it (our data changes quite a bit and there are constant data quality issues -- pointblank helps us A LOT in this regard and its honestly a lifesaver)

title: More languages to add to make it more usable for more people
description: Aside from the 5 languages you have now, would you consider adding a few more? Some that I think would be good are Portuguese, Dutch, Danish, Czech, and Polish. Thank you.

title: Additional language support for message parts
description: I really like that you added multilingual support for the report outputs. One place where that is currently missing (I think) is in the stock message parts for the emailing of the pointblank report. Could you add those in?

title: Include a notification function that integrates with Slack
description:
Thanks for making this package! It's very helpful and I got a few validation processes running smoothly in production (no issues with that at all).

I like the email notifier that's included and something along the same lines is a Slack notifier, which would be a great addition! Would that be a feature you're willing to add in?

title: Refactor the `create_autobrief()` util function
description: This function could use some refactoring and tidying up.

title: Add print method for the x-list
description: As a way to make the x-list object a bit more visually appealing in the console (and less annoying), a print method should be added.

title: Add autobrief functionality for the `conjointly()` validation step function
description: The `conjointly()` function does not currently create an `autobrief` if `brief = NULL` (which is most of the time). So, handcraft a nice brief that states the number of steps and the types of validations contained in this step. Limit the listing of validation types to three.

title: Include console messages that show progress of interrogation
description: Right now, nothing in shown in the console during an interrogation (or even at the conclusion of one). So, use messages to convey what is happening.

title: Have options to sort agent report by failure condition
description: Currently, the agent report provides line entries for all validation steps in the given order. There should be options for sorting by severity of the failure conditions and limiting/omitting the passing steps. This will make for more succinct reporting especially in an email context.

title: Add documentation that explains the agent x-list
description: Add documentation for the x-list object. It can take multiple forms, which is potentially confusing. However, good docs and examples can make things more clear.

title: Add functions useful for action levels and `end_fns`
description:
These are functions that perform logging, emailing, and issuing warnings/errors.

Also, there should be variants that create function templates for each of the types.

title: Add support for sparklyr and add tests for interrogations on Spark tables
description: Tables that are `tbl_spark` are not yet supported but this shouldn't be difficult to implement. There will also need to be tests for performing **pointblank** validations on `tbl_spark` datasets.

title: Add an `active` option to all validation step functions
description:
Each validation step function will get the argument `active`, which will accept a logical value (defaulting to `TRUE`).

If step functions are working with an agent, `FALSE` will make the step inactive (still reporting its presence and keeping indexes for the steps unchanged).

If the step functions are operating directly on data, then any step with `active = FALSE` will simply pass the data through, no longer acting as a filter (internally, just returning the data early).

A valid use case for this is setting a global switch on some or all validation steps depending on the context (e.g., in production or not).

title: Reporting across interrogations
description:
I've been using this package (along with your gt package!) for about a month and it's really helped out a lot at work. We're trying to get our data quality under control and this package solves that problem perfectly (it's actually amazing how everything just seems to work without problems).

A feature request that I have is making a sort of combined report of interrogations for the same table but at different times. We want to have these to see (in a simple table) where things have improved or gotten worse.

I honestly wouldn't be surprised if you weren't thinking about this already, so, if this is something you were planning it would be a great next step.

Thank you so much for all your great packages. You're making my life easier!

title: Fix the `rows_distinct()` function for `tbl_dbi` objects
description: Currently this doesn't work for `tbl_dbi` objects (tested on SQLite and MySQL) but it's fine for `data.frame` and `tbl_df`.

title: Have some of the step functions use columns (not just numbers) as comparisons
description:
Love this package! I'm setting up all sorts of validations and one thing I think would be useful is to enable a direct comparison of one column to another.

For example if we wanted to validate that column a is always greater than column b, we should be able to use `col_vals_gt(vars(a), vars(b))`. What do you think?

Again, this package is incredible. Thanks!

title: Improve the reporting produced by `get_agent_report()`
description: Right now, it's a pretty barebones report.

title: Use a `values` list column in the `validation_set` object
description:
This is needed to simplify the model for validation steps. With a list column we can accommodate any type so any values put in `value`, `set`, and `regex` would simply go into the `values` list column. 

This also makes it easier to have non-numeric comparisons so dates or date-times could then be specified and used.

title: `conjointly()` doesn’t work with `tbl_dbi` objects
description: Because the implementation uses `dplyr::bind_cols()` there is no SQL translation. What should be done instead is to use a join on row indices. Then, we get something that works in all contexts.

title: `focus_on` can fail to get the right local dataframe
description:
Here's an example:
``` r

library(pointblank)
# Copied from the docs, but wrapped in a function
fn <- function() {
  my_df <- data.frame(a = c(5, 4, 3, 5, 1, 2))
  
  agent <- create_agent() %>%
    focus_on(tbl_name = "my_df") %>%
    col_vals_lt(
      column = a,
      value = 6) %>%
    interrogate()
  
  all_passed(agent)
}
fn()
#> Error in get(tbl_name): object 'my_df' not found
```

<sup>Created on 2019-09-21 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

Note that if a `my_df` object existed in the global scope, `focus_on` would use the global object instead. I think this behavior is happening because `focus_on` uses `get` instead of `dynGet` [here](https://github.com/rich-iannone/pointblank/blob/1eca023d41cfd2c775b961f53d3ef665c3534c9a/R/focus_on.R#L140).

title: Checks for sf-objects
description:
I intended to check key-properties of `sf(c)`-objects making use of `rows_not_duplicated()`. The check was supposed to ignore the geometry column of the object (cf. 2nd example in reprex).

It seems that `interrogate()` ran into an error, because of the way, `summarize()` works on these objects.

Reprex example:
``` r
library(pointblank)
library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.6.1, GDAL 2.1.3, PROJ 4.9.3

# Geometry object with 2 features
g <- rep(st_sfc(st_point(1:2)), 2)

# vector with 2 entries
v <- c("a", "b")

# object including both objects
mixed_obj <- st_sf("vector" = v, "points" = g)
mixed_obj
#> Simple feature collection with 2 features and 1 field
#> geometry type:  POINT
#> dimension:      XY
#> bbox:           xmin: 1 ymin: 2 xmax: 1 ymax: 2
#> epsg (SRID):    NA
#> proj4string:    NA
#>   vector      points
#> 1      a POINT (1 2)
#> 2      b POINT (1 2)

agent <- create_agent()
agent %>% 
  focus_on("mixed_obj") %>% 
  rows_not_duplicated() %>% 
  interrogate()
#> Error: Can't coerce element 2 from a list to a double

# It already happens, when I only check if column "vector" is duplicated 
# (likely because `sf`-objects have "sticky geometries")
agent <- create_agent()
agent %>% 
  focus_on("mixed_obj") %>% 
  rows_not_duplicated(cols = vector) %>% 
  interrogate()
#> Error: Can't coerce element 2 from a list to a double
```

<sup>Created on 2019-02-12 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

I think it happens at the following chunk in `interrogate()` in the section "# Judge tables on expectation of non-duplicated rows":
```r      
      # Get total count of rows
      row_count <-
        table %>%
        dplyr::group_by() %>%
        dplyr::summarize(row_count = n()) %>%
        dplyr::as_tibble() %>%
        purrr::flatten_dbl()
```

My expectation would be, that

1. in the first case of the reprex (`rows_not_duplicated()`, without specifying columns) each whole row, including the geometry column, would be compared with the others.
2. in the second case (`rows_not_duplicated(cols = vector)`) the check would be done only for the column "vector".

Perhaps a solution might be to call `as_tibble()` before `group_by()` and `summarize()`?

CC: @krlmlr

title: lubridate not installed with package
description: lubridate is required for creation of the HTML summary but is not required on package install.

title: col_exists handling of multiple columns
description:
The description for col_exists implies that it can handle multiple columns. However the method for doing this is not apparent. 

`col_exists(column = c(start_date, age))` looks for a column called "c(start_date, age)"

`col_exists(column = c("start_date", "age"))` looks for a column called c('start_date', 'age')

Given this function isn't fully documented I'm not sure if I'm missing something. Is there a way to pass a vector of column names to this function?

title: Add functionality for simple validations (e.g., `df %>% col_vals_gt(...)`)
description:
The idea is to pass a data object directly to a validation function and get a re-usable output (e.g., vector of logical values) that can be used in other functions. This would be very useful for joint validations where we could have:

```r
df %>% <validation_function>(...) & 
df %>% <validation_function>(...)
```
And the resultant vector of logicals could show which rows jointly passed (of course, one has to ensure that the input is passed to the validation functions unchanged). 

This shouldn't affect the existing API that much. The first argument of any validation function will change from `agent` to `...` where each function will internally sort out whether to use an agent object or immediately interrogate. The `...` will also be useful if we decide to wrap inputs in some helper function (e.g., `jointly()`, etc.).

title: all_passed and n_passed handle NA values differently for some interrogation tests
description:
Different parts of the interrogration report handle NA values differently. This is apparent for col_vals_between and col_vals_in_set (as well as presumably effecting other tests I don't currently use).

I have a simple dataframe that includes missing values and check that all values of column B are between 0 and 20.
```
df<-structure(list(A = c(NA, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, NA, 8L, 9L, NA), 
               B = c(11L, 12L, NA, NA, NA, NA, 17L, 18L, 19L, 20L), 
               C = c(NA, NA, NA, 24L, NA, 26L, NA, 28L, NA, 30L)), 
               .Names = c("A",  "B", "C"), row.names = c(NA, -10L), class = "data.frame")

agent <-
  create_agent() %>%
  focus_on(tbl_name = "df") %>%
    col_vals_between( 
    column = B,
    left = 0,
    right = 20)
  interrogate()

all_passed(agent)
get_interrogation_summary(agent)
```

`all_passed()` returns `TRUE` but `get_interrogation_summary()` reports that 60% of rows are not within range. 

```
# A tibble: 1 x 12
  tbl_name db_type  assertion_type   column value regex all_passed     n n_passed f_passed action brief            
  <chr>    <chr>    <chr>            <chr>  <dbl> <chr> <lgl>      <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>  <chr>            
1 df       local_df col_vals_between B         NA NA    TRUE          10        6      0.6 NA     Expect that valu~
```

This occurs because the NAs are counted as failing in some calculations but not in others. 

I can partially control this behaviour by adding a pre-condition to only apply this test to rows where B is not NA.

```
agent <-
  create_agent() %>%
  focus_on(tbl_name = "df") %>%
  col_vals_between(
    column = B,
    left = 0,
    right = 20,
    preconditions = is.na(B) == FALSE) %>%
  interrogate()
```
But this becomes tedious when applying testing a large number of columns where NAs should not be counted as failing (since each would require a pre-condition that refers to the relevant column by name).  

It's also not apparent whether I could specify that NAs should be counted as **not** in range (except by using a different test). This is a problem if I want the to trigger a warning or notification based on the joint failure rate of NAs and out of range values.

The ability to include or exclude NAs from any given test (as in the example below)  would improve the usability of this function and add consistency between the n_passed and all_passed values.

```
agent <-
  create_agent() %>%
  focus_on(tbl_name = "df") %>%
  col_vals_between(
    column = B,
    left = 0,
    right = 20,
    na_as_in_range = TRUE) %>%
  interrogate()
```

title: col_values_in_set passes even when values are not in the set
description:
The `col_values_in_set ` test appears to pass regardless of whether or not values are actually in the set. See reproducible example below:

Create a simple two column data frame

```
df <-
  data.frame(
    a = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
    b = c("one", "two", "three", "four"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

Validate that all numerical values in column `a` belong to a numerical set, and, that all values in column `b` belong to a set of string values. Note that _none_ of the values in _either_ validation set should pass.

```
agent <-
  create_agent() %>%
  focus_on(tbl_name = "df") %>%
  col_vals_in_set(
    column = a,
    set = 10:20) %>%
  col_vals_in_set(
    column = b,
    set = c("mouse", "dog", "cat", "pig")) %>%
  interrogate()
```

However, all validation checks are reported as passed
```
all_passed(agent)
[1] TRUE
```

title: Row-based validations in yaml
description:
Support no-argument functions in yaml:

```r
library(pointblank)

p <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml")
writeLines(c(
  "type: agent",
  "tbl: small_table",
  "steps:",
  "- rows_distinct"        # `- rows_distinct: ~` works; this does not
), p)

yaml_read_agent(p)
#> Error: argument is of length zero
```

This matches how these are [documented for python](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/user-guide/yaml/yaml-validation-workflows.html#row-based-validations).

title: YAML documentation
description: It would be helpful to have detailed YAML documentation, even though it mostly comes down to "the functions in this package, but as steps". I've mostly used the [python yaml docs](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/user-guide/yaml/yaml-validation-workflows.html), since they're clearer.

title: Actions vs thresholds
description:
- Python: `thresholds` keyword, values `warning`, `error`, `critical`
- R: `actions` / `action_levels` keyword, levels `warn_at`, `stop_at`, `notify_at` (but I think maybe the python names also work?)

Step-level values replace global rather than merging (so if `warn_at` is set at step level but other levels aren't and othr levels are set globally, the other values don't apply). I'm not sure whether that's the same in python, but Claude was confused by it and I think I agree.

title: `pattern` vs `regex` in `col_vals_regex()`
description: R `col_vals_regex()` has an argument `regex`, python `col_vals_regex()` has `pattern`. In a YAML spec, both should be accepted. Presumably the translation should happen between loading a spec and applying it.

title: Alias `col_vals_lte` / `col_vals_gte`
description: Python uses `col_vals_le` and `col_vals_ge`, R uses `col_vals_lte` and `col_vals_gte`. Add aliases for the Python versions.
